# Herdr metadata panel: drop duplicate ID row from data section

## Problem statement

In the herdr work item selection list, the metadata panel for the selected item shows the work item ID twice: once in the panel title/header line (`── WL-XXXX ──`) and again as the first row of the metadata data table (`ID  WL-XXXX`). The ID row in the data table is redundant and should be dropped, leaving the ID only in the panel title line.

## Users

Users navigating work items in the herdr selection list (`prefix+l`).

**User story:** As a user browsing work items in the herdr selection list, I want the item ID shown once in the metadata panel so the panel is not redundant and the layout is cleaner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The metadata data table in the herdr metadata panel no longer contains an `ID` row.
- [ ] The metadata panel title/header line (`── WL-XXXX ──`) still shows the item ID.
- [ ] Other metadata rows (Status, Stage, Priority, Title, etc.) render unchanged.
- [ ] The detail view (`formatDetailContent`) behavior is unchanged (it already omits ID/Title from its table since they appear in its header).
- [ ] Tests are added/updated covering the metadata panel output (e.g. the `formatMetadataPanel` describe block in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Fix should follow the existing pattern used by the detail view (`formatDetailContent` filters `ID`/`Title` out of the table since they are in the header).
- No behavior change to the CLI `show` output or other renderers.

## Existing state

`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`:

- `formatMetadataPanel` (line ~874) renders the panel header separator `── ${item.id} ──` (line ~891) and then the metadata table from `buildMetaRows(item)` (line ~894).
- `buildMetaRows` (line ~828) unconditionally adds the ID as the first row via `addMeta('ID', item.id)` (line ~835).
- The detail view `formatDetailContent` (line ~969) already filters `ID` and `Title` out of the shared table because both appear in its header: `.filter(([label]) => label !== 'ID' && label !== 'Title')`.

So the metadata panel currently shows the ID in both the header line and the first data row — the inconsistency with the detail view.

## Desired change

Remove the `ID` row from the metadata table rendered in the metadata panel, consistent with how `formatDetailContent` handles it. The header line `── WL-XXXX ──` continues to display the ID. The `Title` row should remain in the metadata panel table since the panel header does not show the title.

Likely approach: in `formatMetadataPanel`, filter the `ID` row from `buildMetaRows(item)` output (e.g. `.filter(([label]) => label !== 'ID')`), mirroring `formatDetailContent`. Alternatively, remove `addMeta('ID', item.id)` from `buildMetaRows` — but note `formatDetailContent` relies on `buildMetaRows` including ID then filtering it, so removing it from the shared builder is also safe as long as tests are updated. Prefer the filter-in-panel approach for minimal blast radius.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `formatMetadataPanel` (~line 874) and/or `buildMetaRows` (~line 828); the ID row is added at line ~835.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — `formatMetadataPanel — field rendering and scrolling` describe block (~line 896); add a test asserting the data table no longer contains an `ID` row while the header still shows the ID. Existing test `expect(joined).toContain('WL-RICH1')` may still pass via the header, but a negative assertion is needed.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X** — "Herdr plugin: reserve bottom 40% of selection list for item metadata and last command" (completed): introduced the metadata panel and shared `buildMetaRows` (origin of the ID duplication).
- **WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9** — "Herdr selection list: metadata section should use the same icons as the list section" (open): also touches metadata section presentation.
- **WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3** — "Show description preview in herder plugin selection list" (open): related to the selection list metadata area.
- **WL-0MNK7CB3F0008YT3** — "Display work item ID in TUI metadata block" (completed): the deprecated Blessed-TUI predecessor; closed as wont-fix/deprecated — not to be used as a pattern.

(Note: an automated find-related scan flagged WL-0MQCU6R6V008JX62, WL-0MRERDU1J000W1IS, WL-0MM0DBM6I1PHQBFI and README worktree copies; these were false positives from keyword overlap and are not genuinely related — excluded per conservative policy.)

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: "metadata section" refers to the herdr selection-list metadata panel (the only place showing the ID both in a title line and as the first data-table row). The CLI `show` output shows ID once in its metadata table with no separate ID-bearing title line, so it is out of scope.
- Low risk: change is localized; detail view and CLI outputs are unaffected.
- Scope creep: do not change icon consistency (tracked by WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9) or add description previews (tracked by WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3) in this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which metadata section is this about?" — Answer (user): "The metadata section has the ID in the title line and in the first line of the data section. Drop it from the data section." Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: the herdr metadata panel, whose title line is `── <id> ──` and whose first data-table row is `ID  <id>`. Verified against `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (lines 891 and 835).
- Q: "Should the Title row remain in the metadata panel table?" — Assumption (agent, Map): Yes — the panel header shows only the ID, not the title, so Title is not duplicated and stays. Source: code inspection of `formatMetadataPanel` header (line 891 shows only `item.id`). Documented in Desired change.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MMOME4VU181A4GP** – Show risk and effort scores int he meta-data (completed)
- **WL-0MMS4EVBA03V6PT4** – Deterministic Readiness Parser (completed)
- **WL-0MSEPP1QC005UL0K** – Documentation updates (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0msaynvby006lm9x, acceptance, add, adds, again (+158 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: add, added, adds, again, agent (+132 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: 0mrerdu1j000w1is, 0msfzkql700381p3, 0msgixhhi009kfw9, add, added (+111 more)

data.description: When install-herdr.sh appends the [[keys.command]] prefix+l -> worklog-selection-list.open-worklist block to ~/.config/herdr/config.toml, the running herdr server keeps its startup keybindings in memory and does not watch the config file (confirmed in herdr v0.7.5 source: config loaded once at startup via Config::load() in server/headless.rs:4202; only server.reload_config re-reads it). The script prints 'Inserted herdr keybinding ...' with no reload hint, so the binding appears dead until the user manually runs 'herdr server reload-config' or restarts the server. Fix: after writing the config, run 'herdr server reload-config' (best-effort, ignore failure) and/or print a clear hint that a reload/restart is required. AC: re-running the installer makes the prefix+l binding immediately active in a running server without manual reload; script still works when no server is running (skip reload gracefully).
data.title: install-herdr.sh should reload herdr config after inserting keybinding

# Intake brief — Unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic across icon display and downtime dispatcher (WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE)

## Problem statement

The audit-freshness predicate (`isAuditFresh` in `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`) is the sole freshness gate for two consumers: the herdr icon display and the downtime dispatch audit tier.  Running an audit atomically bumps the item's `updatedAt` to within milliseconds of `auditedAt` (`saveAuditResult` sets `updatedAt = auditedAt` in the same transaction).  The current freshness comparison must treat the audit's own persistence write as "at-or-near" rather than a strict offset, or the just-persisted audit appears stale to one consumer while fresh to another.  A named tolerance keeps the two consumers in lockstep.

## Users

- **Producer / operator** (MR-0MSIDWS2V007FJRB) — wants `/skill:audit` not to re-dispatch immediately after a fresh audit, and wants the list icon to stop flickering stale right after the run they just persisted.
- **Herdr consumer** (TUI + downtime worker) — both read the same predicate; no competing reimplementation sits in either path.

### User stories

- As a producer who ran `/skill:audit`, I see the fresh audit icon (✅/❌/❓) immediately after the run, not the stale glyph.
- As an operator with downtime dispatch enabled, a just-audited item is not a redundant audit-tier dispatch candidate in the next tick.
- As an engineer touching freshness logic, I change one constant and both consumers follow.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` in `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` treats `auditedAt` **at or near** `updatedAt` within a named tolerance constant as fresh (e.g. `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS`), covering the just-persisted case (`auditedAt ~ updatedAt`, delta well under the tolerance).
2. The current `60000` ms literal is replaced/named by that constant; the project has exactly one freshness definition and tolerance value — neither the icon path (`stageDisplayIcon`/`auditIcon`) nor the dispatch path introduces a competing comparison.
3. A unit test in the `isAuditFresh` suite asserts true (fresh) for a just-persisted audit where `auditedAt` and `updatedAt` differ by milliseconds.
4. A unit test asserts false (stale) for a genuinely stale audit where `updatedAt` is well past `auditedAt`.
5. `selectAuditCandidate` / `getNextAuditCandidate` and `classifyItemForDispatch` (audit branch) in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` continue to import and reuse the same `isAuditFresh` predicate as the sole freshness filter — a just-persisted fresh item is excluded from candidates.
6. Full project test suite passes with the new changes; related docs/comments updated.

## Constraints

- Single source of truth: only `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` defines the predicate and tolerance — downtime and icon paths import it.
- Keep the 7-day recency and `needsProducerReview` filters untouched; only the freshness comparison's shape/tolerance is in scope.
- Tolerances small and documented; do not inflate the window so genuinely post-audit edits appear fresh.
- Backwards compatible: items with missing/unparseable timestamps remain "not fresh" (conservative default, unchanged).

## Existing state

- `isAuditFresh` lives in `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` (`return auditTime > updateTime - 60000`).  Doc comment describes `updatedAt = auditedAt` atomicity (`WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9`) and the `needsProducerReview` no-bump guarantee (`WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R`), but the magic `60000` is unnamed and the comparison direction was not drawn to match the SorraAgents canonical `at-or-near` fix (`SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4`).
- Dispatch path (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) imports `isAuditFresh` in `selectAuditCandidate` and `classifyItemForDispatch` (audit branch).  `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_RECENCY_WINDOW_MS` (7 days) and the stale `auditStaleIcon` handling are orthogonal and stay.
- Tests pin the icon and dispatcher but no pinned case asserts `auditedAt ~ updatedAt` with a 0–50 ms delta as fresh.

## Desired change

- Derive a named tolerance constant `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS` (scope — `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`) whose value follows the SorraAgents canonical fix; reconcile the comparison shape (`auditTime > updateTime - buffer`) with the canonical at-or-near semantics (confirm target semantics with the operator before locking the milling direction).
- Route **both** consumers through the same imported predicate; no secondary comparison is added in `downtime-worker.ts` or the icon path.
- Add/extend unit tests for the two shapes required by the ACs (milliseconds-near → fresh; genuinely stale → stale) and for dispatcher exclusion of a just-persisted fresh item.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — Defines `isAuditFresh` and `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS`; the comparison shape and tolerance are drawn to the at-or-near semantics so `auditedAt ~ updatedAt` is fresh.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Audit-tier `selectAuditCandidate` / `getNextAuditCandidate` and `classifyItemForDispatch` (audit branch) import and reuse `isAuditFresh` as the sole freshness filter; verified that just-persisted items are excluded.
- `packages/herdr/src/icons.test.ts` / `tests/unit/icons.test.ts` — Unit tests for `isAuditFresh` covering near-simultaneous and stale deltas and the icon/dispatcher exclusion property.
- `docs/dev/audit-freshness.md` (if present) — Updated to name the canonical at-or-near tolerance and single-source-of-truth import rule.

## Related work

- discovered-from: `SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4` (SorraAgents audit_runner) — canonical at-or-near reference implementation.
- related-to: `WL-0MSI9FK2Q0074C31` Audit candidate selection, `WL-0MSI9WPNI0044R` Audit dispatch tier, parent `WL-0MSI8H3HP700K0RG` Allow /skill:audit on complete/in_review items without a valid audit.
- related-to: `WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9` Audit freshness: atomically persist updatedAt=auditedAt (explains the near-simultaneous bump), `WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R` Flag-only updates don't bump updatedAt.
- follow-up from: `WL-0MTRG4M9Z0021XDC` (prior intake session — brief recorded but `intake_complete` not yet advanced; this session completes it).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — tolerance too large hides real staleness.** Mitigation: keep the constant small (e.g. the SorraAgents canonical 1000 ms / current 60 s envelope) and keep the genuinely-stale regression test.
- **Risk — comparison direction inversion regresses freshness.** Mitigation: confirm canonical direction with operator/SorraAgents implementation before merging; add the two-pattern unit tests (millisecond-near + genuinely stale) as the gate.
- **Risk — second freshness copy introduced on dispatch side.** Mitigation: lint/grep guard in the test suite that there is exactly one `AUDIT_FRESHNESS` / `60 * 1000` literal.
- **Assumption — `saveAuditResult` keeps `updatedAt = auditedAt` atomically** (WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9).  If it changes, the at-or-near predicate still holds (it simply becomes more generous).
- **Scope creep — don't rework the 7-day recency window or producer-review flag.** Record any such drift as a separate work item.

## Open questions

- None — WL requires the canonical at-or-near comparison shape and tolerance to be confirmed with the operator before implementing (see Notes).  Intake records the question for the implement session; the brief does not block on it.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Does the comparison shape `auditTime > updateTime - buffer` already equal the canonical at-or-near semantics, or should it be `|auditedAt - updatedAt| < tolerance`? — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — confirm with producer and the SorraAgents SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4 fix before implementing; current brief calls it out as a reconcile step. Evidence: description Notes "Reconcile the comparison shape … Confirm the target semantics with the operator before implementing."
- Q: What tolerance value should be canonically named? — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — proposal `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS` at or near the existing 60 s envelope, but final numeric value to be reconciled with the SorraAgents fix (SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4). Evidence: description Notes.

## Interview notes

- Lightweight intake: work item is well-defined with explicit ACs and expected-behaviour text; no operator interview round was needed beyond repo/context search.  Description originates from `herdr-downtime` auto-dispatch discovery (comment WL-C0MTPZ2EBU0000PEG).
data.title: Unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic across icon display and downtime dispatcher

## Problem statement

SorraAgents is the canonical installer for pi agent guidance: its scripts/install_pi.sh symlinks the global guidance (AGENTS_GLOBAL.md -> ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md, plus skills and prompts) into every project. The global AGENTS.md already contains the full agent workflow (work-item lifecycle, implement/build-test-commit order, push policy, triage policy).

ContextHub's 'wl init' (src/commands/init.ts) currently has overlapping responsibilities: it prompts for a workflow choice (promptWorkflowChoice: N / B / M, where M is 'Manage custom workflow by editing AGENTS.md directly') and, via ensureWorkflowTemplateInstalled / insertWorkflowLoaderIntoAgents, can inline WORKFLOW content into the project's AGENTS.md. When the SorraAgents global install is present this creates two sources of truth for agent workflow guidance and can conflict with the canonical global file.

## User story

As a developer running wl init on a machine with the SorraAgents install, I want wl init to delegate agent-guidance/workflow setup to the SorraAgents install so the global guidance is the single source of truth and the project AGENTS.md only carries project-specific content.

## Desired change

- When the SorraAgents global install is detected (i.e. ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md resolves to a SorraAgents AGENTS_GLOBAL.md symlink), wl init should NOT inline workflow content into the project AGENTS.md. Instead it should emit/keep the canonical reference structure used by SorraAgents projects:
  - '## Global agent guidance' section referencing ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md
  - '## Project-specific guidance' section for local rules
- wl init should either invoke the SorraAgents install (scripts/install_pi.sh) or clearly document that the SorraAgents install is the canonical mechanism, rather than duplicating guidance.
- The existing pointer-line behavior from 'wl init: prefer global AGENTS.md pointer' (WL-0MLD6N0GW12MNKK0) must be preserved and aligned with the canonical structure above.
- Standalone Worklog users without the SorraAgents install keep the current workflow options (N/B/M) unchanged.

## Success criteria

1. With the SorraAgents global install present, running wl init in a fresh project does not inline WORKFLOW content into AGENTS.md; the file carries the canonical global-reference structure only.
2. wl init output/help documents the SorraAgents install as the canonical global-guidance mechanism (delegation), with no duplicated workflow content.
3. Without the SorraAgents install, existing wl init workflow behavior (N/B/M) is unchanged and existing tests pass.
4. Tests cover both environments (with and without the global SorraAgents symlink).
5. Full ContextHub test suite passes.

## Related work

- ContextHub: 'wl init: prefer global AGENTS.md pointer' (WL-0MLD6N0GW12MNKK0, completed) established the pointer-line behavior this item extends.
- SorraAgents: 'AGENTS.md installer: emit single reference line for new projects' is the complementary installer-side item; the AGENTS.md split (AGENTS_GLOBAL.md canonical source + symlink install) landed in SA-0MSIUUYRD002GC8W.
data.title: Align wl init with SorraAgents install: delegate agent-guidance/workflow setup instead of duplicating

# Intake Brief: Colour code work items by priority in selection lists (CLI + Herdr)

**Work Item ID:** WL-0MSJ2JFMO007PGQ6

**Headline:** Colour coding of work items in the selection list should be based on **priority**, not stage: critical are red, high are orange, medium is yellow, low is white — recorded in a shared theme file. *(revised 2026-09-08 per producer review)*

## Problem Statement

Work item titles in selection lists are currently coloured by **stage** (progression: gray → blue → cyan → yellow → green → white, from WL-0MQ53H78W000DQ08). Stage progression communicates workflow position, but operators scanning a list need to see **priority** at a glance — critical items should jump out in red, low-priority items should recede. The colour scheme must be defined once in a shared theme file.

## Users

All Worklog users viewing work item lists:

- **Operators and agents** scanning `wl list` / `wl search` / `wl recent` need immediate visual cue of what matters (critical = red, high = orange).
- **Herdr users** browsing the Worklog selection list pane need the same priority cue.

Example user stories:
- "As an operator, I want critical work items to appear red so I can immediately spot what needs attention."
- "As an agent, I want low-priority items dimmed so they recede while scanning the list."
- "As a project manager, I want a consistent priority colour scheme across the CLI and the Herdr selection list, defined in one shared theme file."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The canonical priority colour mapping is recorded in the shared theme file `src/theme.ts`:
   - `critical` → red
   - `high` → orange
   - `medium` → yellow
   - `low` → white  *(revised from white/dimmed per producer review 2026-09-08: medium yellow has better contrast, low white replaces dim)*
2. Work item **titles and ids** are both coloured by **priority** (same colour), everywhere they appear: `wl list`, `wl search`, `wl recent`, `wl show`, `wl next`, and the Herdr worklist selection list (`formatItemLine`).  *(revised per producer review 2026-09-08: ids should share the title's priority colour for a consistent visual cue; original spec had ids by stage)*
3. Blocked items no longer receive the unconditional red override; they are coloured by their natural priority like every other item (per clarification Q3b).
4. Unknown/missing priority falls back to a sensible default colour (medium/yellow) and unknown/missing stage keeps a sensible default (gray) — matching current fallback behaviour.
5. Unit tests cover the new priority colour mapping (title and id both priority-coloured) in both the CLI helpers (`src/commands/helpers.ts`) and the Herdr icons (`packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`), including blocked and unknown-priority cases.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- The Herdr plugin (`packages/herdr/`) is a separate package depending only on `@worklog/shared`; it renders raw ANSI 256-colour escape codes and cannot import `src/theme.ts` (which depends on chalk).
- The Pi-based TUI extension (`packages/tui/`) is **out of scope** — it is slated for removal (see WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N) and colours via Pi theme tokens, not the theme file.
- "Orange" should use a colour consistent with the existing `theme.text.readyNo` (`chalk.hex('#FFA500')`).
- No new dependencies.

## Existing state

- `src/theme.ts` already has a `priority` map (`critical: chalk.redBright`, `high: chalk.yellowBright`, `medium: chalk.blueBright`, `low: chalk.gray`), a `stage` progression map, and a `blocked: chalk.redBright` override.
- `src/commands/helpers.ts` — `renderTitle()` colours the title by stage (`titleColorForStage`), with a blocked override checked first; `formatTitleAndId()` renders the id muted (`theme.text.muted`); `humanFormatWorkItem()` also renders ids muted in several formats.
- Herdr: `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` has `stageColor()` / `applyStageColour()`; `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `formatItemLine()` colours the title by stage and leaves the id uncoloured. `STAGE_COLORS` (worklist.ts) is reused by the stage-filter dialog and separators.

## Desired change

- **`src/theme.ts`:** update `priority` colours to red / orange / yellow / white. Keep the `stage` map (used by the stage filter). Remove the `blocked` override (per Q3b) or leave it unused — implementer decision, but `renderTitle` must no longer apply it.
- **`src/commands/helpers.ts`:** `renderTitle()` colours by priority (fallback for unknown priority); `formatTitleAndId()` and `humanFormatWorkItem()` colour ids by priority (same as title) instead of muted. This automatically covers list, search, recent, show, next. *(ids by priority per producer revision 2026-09-08)*
- **Herdr `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`:** add `priorityColor(priority)` / `applyPriorityColour(text, priority)` using ANSI 256 codes (red ≈ 196, orange ≈ 208, yellow ≈ 220, white ≈ 15). Keep `stageColor` / `applyStageColour` for the stage filter dialog/separators. *(medium 220 / low 15 per producer revision 2026-09-08)*
- **Herdr `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`:** `formatItemLine()` — title and id both via priority colour. Keep `STAGE_COLORS` for the stage filter dialog and separators. *(ids by priority per producer revision 2026-09-08)*
- **Shared theme consideration:** the priority colour *spec* lives in `src/theme.ts`. To prevent drift between the CLI (chalk) and Herdr (ANSI), consider extracting a colour-name spec (e.g. a `packages/shared` module mapping priority → colour name, consumed by both) — at minimum the two maps must stay consistent. Flag as design decision for the implementer; do not over-engineer.

## Key Files:

- `src/theme.ts` — canonical priority colour mapping (red/orange/yellow/white); stage map retained for the stage filter but not for ids *(revised 2026-09-08)*
- `src/commands/helpers.ts` — `renderTitle` (priority colour), `formatTitleAndId` / `humanFormatWorkItem` (priority-coloured ids, same as title)
- `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` — add `priorityColor` / `applyPriorityColour` (ANSI 256)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `formatItemLine` title+id both by priority

## Related work

- **WL-0MQ53H78W000DQ08** (completed, high) — "Refactor colour mappings: remove status-based colours, use stage progression with blocked override". Established the current stage-based scheme this item replaces for titles. See `src/theme.ts`, `src/commands/helpers.ts`.
- **WL-0MQ8LKXH20058N1M** (completed, high) — "Consistent colour scheme for work item titles in Blessed and Pi TUIs". Earlier consistency work; Pi TUI out of scope here.
- **WL-0MP15YIQ200748RC / WL-0MP15YJ4A0031YGR** (completed) — "Implement colour mapping in TUI and CLI" and its test item.
- **WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N** (open, high) — "Remove the Pi-based TUI from the repo; keep the agent-side Pi plugin features" — Pi TUI excluded from this scope.
- **WL-0MSI1LVTJ001M9EY** (open, high) — "Herdr selection list: sort by priority first, then stage" — sibling priority-related change to the same Herdr worklist.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "Selection list" = `wl list` / `wl search` / `wl recent` / `wl show` outputs plus the Herdr worklist pane (confirmed by user: "both a and b plus the herdr plugin").
- **Assumption:** Title = priority colour, id = stage colour, everywhere (confirmed: "Always use priority in title and stage colouring in id (everywhere they appear)").
- **Assumption:** Blocked items show their natural priority colour; the always-red blocked override is removed (confirmed: Q3 answer "b").
- **Risk:** CLI and Herdr colour maps drifting apart → mitigate by keeping both maps in the shared theme spec / one source of truth.
- **Risk:** ANSI 256 approximations of "orange" / "white" / "dim" in Herdr may differ slightly from chalk's named colours → verify visually against the CLI.
- **Scope-creep guard:** Pi TUI colouring, sorting changes (WL-0MSI1LVTJ001M9EY), and other Herdr list features are separate work items and must not be expanded into this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Scope of 'selection list' — should priority-based colours apply to (a) `wl list` / `wl search` / `wl recent`, (b) `wl show` detail view, (c) both?" — Answer (user): "both a and b plus the herdr plugin". Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Priority vs Stage relationship — should priority (a) replace stage as primary colour source, (b) supersede only for title colour keeping stage in metadata, (c) only affect list views?" — Answer (user): "Always use priority in title and stage colouring in id (everywhere they appear)". Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Blocked items — currently `blocked` is a red override that beats stage. Should blocked items (a) still override everything (always red), (b) show their natural priority colour?" — Answer (user): "b". Meaning: blocked items are coloured by their priority like every other item; the unconditional red override in `renderTitle` is removed. Source: interactive reply.


## Revision log

- **2026-09-08 (producer review rgardler):** original ACs specified `medium → white`, `low → dimmed`, ids by stage. Rejected first delivery: ids should use the same colour as the title; low was too dim. Revised mapping: `medium → yellow`, `low → white`; titles **and** ids both coloured by priority (same colour). Implemented in commits f814cdb8 / 8cd160cc / fafaf7de on dev. AC text above reflects the revised spec.

# Auto-downgrade critical priority when item is marked completed/in_review

## Problem statement

A work item that is marked **completed/in_review** can still carry `critical` priority today. Critical is a signal for urgent *open* work — it drives `wl next` ordering, TUI selection lists, and grouping — so a finished item left at critical competes with genuinely urgent items and makes dashboards misleading. When an item transitions to a terminal state (`status=completed` and/or `stage=in_review`), its priority must not remain `critical`.

## Users

- **Operators and agents** who close out work items.
  - *As an operator, when I mark a critical item as completed/in_review, I want its priority automatically downgraded to `high`, so that finished work stops competing with genuinely urgent open items.*
  - *As a developer, I want the automatic downgrade reported in the command output, so that I can verify the change happened.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When a work item with `priority=critical` transitions to a terminal state — `status=completed` or `stage=in_review` (via `wl update`) or `status=completed` (via `wl close`) — its priority is automatically downgraded to `high`.
2. Priorities other than `critical` (`high`, `medium`, `low`) are never modified by a terminal transition.
3. Command output reports the downgrade: a machine-readable field in `--json` output and a summary line in human-readable output, consistent with the existing `downgradedChildren` reporting in `wl update`.
4. Unit tests cover: `wl update --status completed`, `wl update --stage in_review`, `wl close`, and no-op cases (non-critical priorities unchanged; non-terminal transitions like `plan_complete` leave `critical` intact).
5. Full project test suite passes, and `CLI.md` documentation for `wl update` / `wl close` is updated to describe the auto-downgrade behavior.

## Constraints

- Canonical priorities are `critical | high | medium | low` (see `src/validators/priority.ts`); the downgrade target is `high` per operator specification.
- Only terminal transitions trigger the downgrade — moving `critical` items between non-terminal stages (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`) must not touch priority.
- Must not conflict with the existing child cascade: `cascadePriorityDowngrade` in `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (parent downgrade → children). A completed item is itself terminal, so no child cascade is implied by this rule.
- Prefer reusing existing reporting patterns from `src/commands/update.ts` over inventing new output formats.

## Existing state

- The database allows any priority with any status/stage; there is no rule preventing `critical` on completed/in_review items today.
- Terminal transitions are: `wl update <id> --status completed --stage in_review` (`src/commands/update.ts`) and `wl close <id>` (`src/commands/close.ts` sets `status=completed`, `stage=done`).
- A directly related cascade already exists: `cascadePriorityDowngrade(parentId, newPriority)` in `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (line ~1230) downgrades critical *children* to `high` when a parent drops from `critical`, reported via `downgradedChildren` in `src/commands/update.ts` (lines ~383–408).
- `wl doctor` validates status/stage combinations (`src/doctor/status-stage-check.ts`) but has no priority-vs-stage rule.

## Desired change

1. Add a small helper (e.g., `downgradeIfTerminal(updatedItem)` or an inline check alongside the existing cascade) that, when an item is transitioning to a terminal state, downgrades `critical` → `high`.
2. Invoke it from the terminal-transition paths in `src/commands/update.ts` (stage/status changes) and `src/commands/close.ts` (close path). Decide between explicit call sites vs. enforcement inside the shared `update()` — prefer explicit call sites to avoid side effects on internal cascade `update()` calls unless a guard makes it safe.
3. Report downgraded items in JSON and human-readable output, mirroring the `downgradedChildren` pattern.
4. Add unit tests and update `CLI.md`.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/update.ts` — terminal transition handling (`--status completed` / `--stage in_review`); add downgrade enforcement and reporting.
- `src/commands/close.ts` — close path sets `status=completed`; enforce downgrade here too.
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — home of `cascadePriorityDowngrade`; natural location for the new helper (e.g., `downgradeIfTerminal`) if a DB-layer helper is preferred.
- `src/validators/priority.ts` — canonical priority constants to reuse.
- `tests/database.test.ts` (and/or `tests/cli/*`) — unit tests for the new behavior.
- `CLI.md` — document auto-downgrade in `wl update` / `wl close` sections.

## Related work

- `Auto-downgrade critical children when parent priority is reduced (WL-0MS7YCCLV000YJCR)` — completed; the direct precedent: same `critical` → `high` downgrade rule and reporting pattern, but for parent→child cascades.
- `Add priority normalization to create, update and doctor commands (WL-0MP14WFW6001VE3G)` — completed; priority validation infrastructure (`src/validators/priority.ts`).
- `Bubble up critical items (WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C)` — completed; critical-priority semantics in `wl next`.
- `Exclude in-review items from wl next (WL-0ML2TS8I409ALBU6)` — completed; in_review semantics.
- `Demote completed/in_review parent to plan_complete when a child is added (WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6)` — open; sibling rule about terminal-state invariants on parents.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** `wl doctor` detection/fix of legacy `critical` + completed/in_review items is a natural extension but is NOT part of this work item's ACs. If wanted, record as a separate linked work item (`discovered-from:WL-0MSJM4EIV001A0V9`).
- **Over-enforcement risk:** blanket enforcement inside the shared DB `update()` could interfere with internal calls (e.g., the child cascade calls `db.update()`); guard conditions must be precise or enforcement kept at explicit call sites.
- **Assumption:** "completed/in_review" means terminal transitions — `status=completed` and/or `stage=in_review`, plus `stage=done` via `wl close`.
- **Assumption:** the downgrade target is `high`, as explicitly specified by the operator.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: The request ended with `--priority low` — what does it refer to?
  - A (assumed, rgardler): `--priority low` sets the priority of this new work item itself (matching `wl create --priority low` CLI syntax), not the downgrade target — the feature spec explicitly downgrades to `high`. Source: interactive reply; interpretation documented here. If wrong, the item priority is a one-line `wl update` fix.
- No further clarification was needed; the seed context was sufficient to draft the brief (interview skipped per intake skill step 4).

## Summary

`wl sync`'s merge logic can enter a self-sustaining conflict loop that silently corrupts item state. Observed in the field (LP-0MSDRRPV0001TCLX in /home/rgardler/projects/llm): a completed, audit-approved item's local `updatedAt` advanced at every sync (21:36:19Z → 21:53:40Z → 21:57:35Z) and the final sync chose a local `deleted` state (empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`) over the remote `open` state — soft-deleting the item while the remote `worklog/data` ref still had it `open`/`plan_complete`. No agent ran `wl delete`; the state arose purely from merge behavior. The item had to be manually restored via `StatusLifecycle`.

## Root-cause hypothesis (verified against src/sync.ts)

1. **Same-timestamp merge bumps `updatedAt` unconditionally.** `mergeSameTimestampItems` (src/sync.ts ~L423) sets `merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` whenever local and remote have the same `updatedAt` but different content (e.g. a `sortIndex` conflict from concurrent `wl re-sort`, or any divergent field). This bump makes the item *newer* than the remote on the next sync, so the local value keeps winning and the timestamp keeps advancing on every sync — a conflict loop with no real user edit behind it. Under auto-sync / multi-pane / multi-agent use this can repeat indefinitely.

2. **Unattributed soft-delete wins over a live remote item.** `deleteSingle` (node_modules/@worklog/shared/src/database.ts) sets `status: 'deleted'` but leaves `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` empty. In `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`, `status` is resolved by plain timestamp recency: `status='deleted'` is a non-default value, so if the local copy is (artifactually) newer, `status` flips to `deleted` even though `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` are empty — silently soft-deleting an item the remote still considers open. There is no delete-side equivalent of the close-preservation logic that protects `status='completed'`/`stage='done'`.

## Expected behaviour

- Repeated syncs of the same divergent state must converge: once both sides hold the merged item, `updatedAt` must stop advancing and the item must not flip-flop.
- An unattributed delete marker (status='deleted' with empty deletedBy/deleteReason) must never override a remote item that is open/in-progress/completed. Deletes should only propagate when they are real, attributed deletes (non-empty deletedBy or deleteReason), mirroring the close-preservation model.

## Suggested approach

- In `mergeSameTimestampItems`, only bump `updatedAt` when the merge actually changed a user-visible field (or converge without bumping when the merged result equals one side). Consider whether `sortIndex` conflicts alone should bump at all.
- Add delete-side protection in `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` (and same-timestamp path): treat `status='deleted'` like `status='completed'` — require the delete to be the newer change AND attributed (deletedBy/deleteReason non-empty) before propagating it; otherwise keep the remote live status.
- Add regression tests in tests/sync.test.ts reproducing both failure modes.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` (differing only in `sortIndex` or one metadata field) synced repeatedly converge — `updatedAt` stops advancing after the merged state is present on both sides (no unbounded bumping).
- AC2: Regression test: local `status='deleted'` with empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` vs remote `status='open'` — merge keeps the remote `open` state (or at minimum never produces a soft-deleted item with no attribution).
- AC3: Regression test: an *attributed* delete (non-empty `deletedBy`) that is newer than the remote still propagates (delete remains possible when intentional).
- AC4: Full existing test suite (npm test) passes with no regressions.
data.title: Fix sync-conflict loop: same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt indefinitely and unattributed soft-delete wins over remote open item

# Sort in_review items in the Herdr selection list (WL-0MSLPM5ZB003TADT) — Intake Brief

## Problem statement

The `In Review` section of the Herdr selection list is ordered only by priority today, so producers and agents must scan the entire review queue to find actionable items; the desired behaviour is a deterministic sub-sort within the `In Review` group that surfaces the most urgent items first, using audit and flag state: `needsProducerReview=true` → fresh failed audit → stale failed audit → no audit → stale passed audit → remaining fresh passed audits.

## Users

- **Producers reviewing the queue** — scan the `In Review` section to decide what to review/close next.
  - *Story:* As a producer, I want failed audits (fresh first, then stale) at the top of `In Review` so the most problematic items are not buried behind un-audited or passed items.
- **Agents/dispatcher selecting review work** — pick the most urgent in_review item to act on.
  - *Story:* As an agent browsing the Herdr list, I want `needsProducerReview` items first, then failed audits, so producer-blocked work is surfaced first and the dispatcher consumes the correct head.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — In-Review bucket order (6 buckets):** Within the single last-positioned `In Review` group (`stage=in_review` items after regrouping), items are rendered in exactly this producer-confirmed bucket order: (1) `needsProducerReview=true` (any audit state), (2) fresh `auditResult=false` (`readyToClose=false` with `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)==true`), (3) stale `auditResult=false` (`readyToClose=false` with `isAuditFresh==false` and `auditedAt` present), (4) no audit (`auditResult==null` or `auditedAt==null`), (5) stale `auditResult=true` (`readyToClose=true` with `isAuditFresh==false`), (6) remaining fresh `auditResult=true`. Within each bucket, items are sorted by priority `high → medium → low`, then by `id` as a deterministic tie-break.
- [ ] **AC2 — Mirrored ordering (Herdr + CLI + list):** The same bucket order applies in all `In Review` renderings: the Herdr regrouped worklist (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` `regroupWorkItems`), `wl next --groups` (`src/commands/grouping.ts`), and `wl list` stage-filtered In Review queries (`wl list --stage in_review` via `src/commands/list.ts` / shared list ordering). Any view that renders the `In Review` section uses the identical bucket predicate.
- [ ] **AC3 — No cross-group regression:** Non-`in_review` groups (`Critical Group N`, `Group N`, `Idea`, `Other`) keep their existing group order and within-group sort (`in_progress → plan_complete → intake_complete → remaining`, then priority). Exactly one `In Review` section still renders, positioned last, with no duplicate headings.
- [ ] **AC4 — Freshness uses `isAuditFresh`:** `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`, 60 s buffer) is the sole freshness predicate; flag-only flips of `needsProducerReview` do not make an audit stale (per WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R), and `auditedAt == updatedAt` atomics keep an immediately-audited item fresh. Stale buckets require `auditedAt` present; absence is the "no audit" bucket, not stale.
- [ ] **AC5 — Tests & docs:** Unit tests cover every bucket (fresh-failed, stale-failed, no audit, stale-passed, fresh-passed, plus `needsProducerReview` precedence) with priority and `id` tie-break within a bucket, plus regroup/list integration tests that the merged Herdr list, `wl next`, and `wl list --stage in_review` all honour the bucket order; grouping comments/README note the 6-bucket order and reference this work item.
- [ ] **AC6 — Duplicate coverage:** `WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV` requirements are fully subsumed by this item's ACs; close `WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV` as a duplicate of this item.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes** with the new ordering, including `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`, `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts`, and list/next command tests.

> Standard criteria also apply:
> - All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
> - Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Keep bucket logic pure and dependency-free inside the sort path (same duplication rationale as `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — Herdr has zero npm deps; a mirrored implementation is required in `src/commands/grouping.ts`/`list.ts`/`next.ts` so Herdr and CLI render identically).
- Reuse `isAuditFresh` from `@worklog/shared/icons` — do not re-implement freshness.
- Do not change how `In Review` membership is decided (still `stage=in_review` regardless of `status`/`priority`); this item only reorders inside the group.

## Existing state

- Herdr `In Review` today holds all `stage=in_review` items (critical-excluded) as a single group rendered last, sorted by `compareGroupableItems` (stage tie → priority → `id`); no audit/flag bucketing.
- `WorkItem` carries `needsProducerReview?: boolean`, `auditResult?: boolean|null`, `auditedAt?: string|null`, `updatedAt?: string`; `normalizeItem` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` and `src/commands/helpers.ts`/`grouping.ts`) populates them and `isAuditFresh` (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`) defines staleness (`auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`).
- `assignItemGroups`/`regroupWorkItems` (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`) and `src/commands/grouping.ts` implement group order `Critical Group N → Group N → Idea → Other → In Review`; `selectWorkItems`/`fetchNextItems` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) compose the final displayed list preserved by regrouping.
- `WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV` ("Sort in_review items in the section list by audit status", `open`, `medium`, `sortIndex 7300`) described a compatible but incomplete bucket phrasing (`needsProducerReview → missing audit → stale → passed`) that omitted the fresh/stale-failed distinction; per producer confirmation it is a duplicate of this item and should be closed.
- `wl list --stage in_review` today returns `isAuditFresh`-agnostic order; `wl next --groups` groups `In Review` but does not bucket-sort it.
- Related past fixes: `WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW` (duplicate In Review sections + group order), `WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW` (in_review stage filter), `WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9` (atomic `auditedAt=updatedAt`).

## Desired change

- Extend the `In Review` rendering order so that after the canonical group assignment, items inside group `In Review` are stable-sorted by the 6-bucket order `(needsProducerReview → fresh-failed → stale-failed → no audit → stale-passed → fresh-passed)` with secondary `priority` + `id` ordering. Apply it in: (a) the Herdr regroup path (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` `regroupWorkItems` / new `compareInReviewItems` helper used for the In Review slice), (b) the CLI grouping path (`src/commands/grouping.ts` + `src/commands/next.ts` grouping emission), and (c) the CLI list path (`src/commands/list.ts` or the shared list sort) so `wl list --stage in_review` renders the same order. Keep the overall contracts (no filtering, deterministic ordering, mandatory items preserved) and ensure Herdr and CLI agree.
- Close `WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV` as a duplicate once coverage is verified.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — `regroupWorkItems` extension + new `inReviewBucket`/`compareInReviewItems` helper for the 6-bucket order; primary fix location.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` — bucket-order tests for all 6 buckets, priority/`id` tie-break, plus regroup integration test.
- `src/commands/grouping.ts` — mirrored `inReviewBucket`/`compareInReviewItems` for CLI grouping so `wl next --groups` matches Herdr.
- `src/commands/list.ts` (+ shared list-sort helper if used) — apply same bucket order for `wl list --stage in_review` (and any filtered list rendering In Review).
- `src/commands/next.ts` — ensure grouped `In Review` emission honours the bucket order.
- `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` — mirrored CLI bucket-order tests.
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` freshness predicate (reference; atomic updatedAt=auditedAt behaviour).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `WorkItem` `needsProducerReview`/`auditResult`/`auditedAt` population via `normalizeItem` (reference; field availability).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — extend if In Review rendering order is asserted there.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` and grouping code comments — document the 6-bucket In Review order.

## Related work

- **WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV** — "Sort in_review items in the section list by audit status" (`open`, `medium`) — duplicate intent confirmed by producer; to be closed as `duplicate` of this item (this brief subsumes its requirements; its `needsProducerReview → missing → stale → passed` phrasing is a shorthand for the full 6-bucket order defined here).
- **WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW** — "Herdr plugin: fix work item list grouping (duplicate In Review sections, wrong group order)" (`completed`, `medium`) — established the single last-positioned `In Review` section and Critical/Group N file-path grouping preserved here.
- **WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW** — "Herdr: in_review stage filter (f-r) shows 0 items because stage-filtered fetch restricts to status=open" (`completed`, `high`) — established that `in_review` items carry `completed`/`in-progress` status and must be fetched specially.
- **WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9 / WL-0MTHRW3770014H51** — atomic `saveAuditResult: updatedAt=auditedAt` and `isAuditFresh` 60 s window; governs the fresh vs stale distinction used by buckets 2/3/5/6.
- **WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2** — "Dispatcher consumes Herdr selection list head" (`in-progress`, `critical`) — dispatcher that will consume the newly-ordered head; consuming the sorted In Review order is the downstream value.
- **WL-0MSNI6TQ5003JY1Z** — narrow-pane header truncation (`in_review`, `high`, `needsProducerReview:true`) — unrelated rendering concern, noted only to avoid chrome-budget interaction.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Stale vs fresh failed precedence:** Producer confirmed that fresh failed (`readyToClose=false` + fresh) outranks stale failed, and stale failed outranks `no audit`; stale passed outranks only the fresh-passed rest. Assumption: within each bucket, priority `high→medium→low` then `id` is the tie-break (from WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV's "within each group sort by priority").
- **Scope-creep risk:** Stage/priority changes inside `In Review`, new `In Review` splitting across multiple headings, or changing membership (e.g. filtering by `needsProducerReview`) are out of scope; record as linked follow-ups, not in-scope.
- **Duplication maintenance:** CLI grouping and Herdr grouping must mirror the same bucket helper to avoid divergence (same rationale as Q2c duplication); keep the logic pure and tested in both places.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What is the exact bucket order inside `In Review`? The description lists needsProducerReview=true first, then audit with readyToClose=false, then no audit, then stale audit, then the rest — but related WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV phrases it as needsProducerReview=true, followed by audit missing, followed by audit stale then audit passed (no mention of the readyToClose=false bucket). Please confirm the canonical 5-bucket order and whether stale-failed and stale-passed both belong in the stale bucket or if failed audits should always outrank stale audits." — Answer (producer 2026-09-04): "needsProducerReview=true → audit readyToClose=false → stale-failed → no audit → stale-passed → rest". Interpretation applied: 6 buckets = `needsProducerReview` → fresh `readyToClose=false` → stale `readyToClose=false` → no audit → stale `readyToClose=true` → fresh `readyToClose=true` (within each bucket: high→medium→low→id). The first `readyToClose=false` bucket is fresh-failed; the explicit `stale-failed` bucket is stale-failed; stale-passed is stale-passed. Source: interactive reply. Research: inspected `packages/shared/src/icons.ts:279` (`isAuditFresh`), `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` (In Review single-last group), `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (WorkItem fields), `src/commands/grouping.ts` (CLI grouping).
- Q: "Should `needsProducerReview` be a bucket for the whole In Review group or a flag that just bubbles flagged items to the very front regardless of audit status?" — Answer (producer, implied by bucket list): it is the topmost bucket covering the whole group — any `needsProducerReview=true` item precedes every non-flagged In Review item regardless of audit state.
- Q: "Does the bucket order apply only to the Herdr plugin or also to `wl next --groups` / CLI In Review rendering?" — Answer (producer 2026-09-04): "wl next mirrors" — CLI grouping mirrors the Herdr bucket order so both render identically.
- Q: "Should `wl list --stage in_review` and the `--priority`/`--status` filtered lists also apply the same In Review bucket order, or only the default/browse worklist?" — Answer (producer 2026-09-04): "wl list shows same ordering" — the same 6-bucket order applies to `wl list` In Review renderings.
- Q: "WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV describes a near-duplicate sort for in_review items. Should it be closed as a duplicate of this item after intake, or kept as a separate follow-up?" — Answer (producer 2026-09-04): "close as duplicate (check this item covers all requirements)" — WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV closes as duplicate of this item; this brief explicitly subsumes its requirements (see AC6 and Related work).
- Additional related docs inspected: `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`, `src/commands/grouping.ts`, `src/commands/list.ts`, `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md`, `wl show WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV --json`.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — Extend `regroupWorkItems` with `inReviewBucket`/`compareInReviewItems` for the 6-bucket Herdr In Review order (`needsProducerReview → fresh-failed → stale-failed → no audit → stale-passed → fresh-passed`, priority/`id` tie-break).
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` — Add 6-bucket and priority tie-break tests + merged-list In Review bucket integration test.
- `src/commands/grouping.ts` + `src/commands/next.ts` — Mirror the same bucket helper for `wl next --groups` CLI In Review grouping.
- `src/commands/list.ts` — Apply the same bucket order for `wl list --stage in_review` filtered In Review rendering.
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` freshness predicate (reference; atomic updatedAt=auditedAt).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `WorkItem` `needsProducerReview`/`auditResult`/`auditedAt` population via `normalizeItem`.

# Prevent top line info bar from scrolling off screen (WL-0MSNI6TQ5003JY1Z)

## Headline

Fix the Herdr plugin's top `Work Items` info bar wrapping off screen in narrow panes by truncating the header to the terminal width so it never exceeds one row.

## Problem statement

In the Herdr `worklog-selection-list` plugin's list mode, the top info bar (row 0: `Work Items — N item(s) [auto-refresh on] [Downtime Off]` plus optional `(filtered: …)`, `(top …)`, `[paused — hidden]` and code-freeze banners) can exceed the pane width in narrow terminals. The header is assembled by string concatenation without truncation, so when its visible length exceeds `cols` the terminal wraps it onto extra physical rows. When total rendered output then exceeds the `rows - 1` line-count invariant (WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO), the terminal scrolls the first line off the top of the pane and the header is not visible — even with the minimal `[Downtime Off]` status and no idle timestamp.

## Users

- **Herdr worklist users** browsing the selection list in narrow panes (e.g. 80 cols or less, `herdr pane layout` narrow split), who rely on the top bar to see the item count, active filter, auto-refresh and downtime state.

### Example User Stories

- As a Herdr user with a narrow pane and many items, I want the top `Work Items` info bar to stay visible at row 0 regardless of pane width or list content, so I don't lose the item count and system status.
- As a Herdr user, I want a long header (filter + auto-refresh + downtime) to be truncated with an ellipsis rather than wrapping onto a second row and pushing the header off screen.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Header never wraps / always visible at row 0:** In list mode, the header line is truncated to fit the terminal width (visible length ≤ `cols`, ANSI preserved via `truncateLine`) so it occupies exactly one output row. For any `cols` ≥ 40 and any combination of `filterLabel`, `totalCount` (`top N of M`), `autoRefresh`, `panePaused`, and `downtimeStatus` (`[Downtime Off]`, `[Downtime Off (restored)]`, `[downtime paused]`, `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]`, `[downtime busy]`, `[⏳ downtime dispatching]`), `renderer(…)` output satisfies `stripAnsi(output.split('
')[0]).includes('Work Items')` and `stripAnsi(output.split('
')[0]).length <= cols`.

2. **Line-count invariant holds in narrow panes:** In list mode the full renderer output contains at most `rows - 1` newline-separated lines for any `TermSize` (e.g. 40×24, 80×24, 120×53, 60×20) and any list state (short list, full list, scrolled list, with/without banners, with/without fold indicators `▲/▼ more`, with minimal and maximal header length). No render exceeds the pane height and the top line is never scrolled off.

3. **No regression in other modes:** Detail-mode rendering (`formatDetailView` and renderer detail path with pinned header+ToC) and filter-mode rendering are unchanged — existing tests for the pinned ToC (WL-0MSI28AP80002F5S / WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I), `'keeps the ToC pinned at the top while the document scrolls'`, and filter prompt still pass with no behavior change.

4. **Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`:** Cover (a) header truncation at narrow width — visible length ≤ `cols` and `Work Items` text still present for a long header at 40 cols and 60 cols; (b) line-count invariant (`lines.length <= rows - 1`) for list mode at narrow width (40×24) with a long header, with banner active, and without banner; (c) wide-pane sanity (80×24 / 120×24) still passes — no over-truncation for short headers.

5. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and any relevant README/docs entries describing the header layout (`packages/herdr/README.md`).**

6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Surgical fix in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `createListRenderer` list-mode header path only — do not change detail/filter rendering or the dynamic list/metadata panel layout beyond the header fix.
- Reuse the existing `truncateLine(line, maxWidth)` helper (ANSI-aware) — no new dependencies or truncation implementations.
- Preserve ANSI styling (bold Work Items, dim/colour for status segments) when truncating; the ellipsis `…` must close open ANSI codes via `ANSI.reset` as `truncateLine` already does.
- Must preserve the `rows - 1` invariant from WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO — the fix must not add chrome rows; the header must remain a single chrome row.
- No change to `renderDowntimeStatus` idle timer growth — truncation must remain correct as the `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]` string grows (regression guard).

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `createListRenderer` (around lines 3217–3229) builds the list-mode header:
  ```ts
  let header = ` ${ANSI.bold}Work Items${ANSI.reset} — ${totalItems} item(s)${filterLabel}`;
  if (totalCount !== undefined && totalCount > totalItems) { header += ` (top ${totalItems} of ${totalCount})`; }
  if (autoRefresh) { header += ` ${ANSI.dim}[auto-refresh on]${ANSI.reset}`; }
  if (panePaused) { header += ` ${ANSI.fg(220)}[paused — hidden]${ANSI.reset}`; }
  if (downtimeStatus) { header += downtimeStatus; }
  output.push(header);
  ```
  The header is pushed without `truncateLine(…, cols)`, unlike banners (`truncateLine(bannerLine, cols)`) and footer/tooltip lines. When `visibleLength(header) > cols`, the pty wraps it onto a second physical row so `output` logically has `rows - 1` lines but physically occupies `rows` or more, scrolling the first line off the top (observed in narrow panes even with minimal `[Downtime Off]` content, and exacerbated by `codeFreezeActive` banners, long `filterLabel` like `(filtered: stage in_review)`, or large `totalCount`).

- Detail view header/ToC is already pinned (WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I / WL-0MSI28AP80002F5S): `formatDetailView` pins `DETAIL_HEADER_LINES + tocLines` at the top and only the body scrolls — not affected by this list-mode header issue.

- Prior fix WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO corrected layout accounting for group separators and notification-line overflow, and WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ accounted for `▲/▼ more` indicators in the `budgetForRows` budget — but neither guarded the header's own width.

- `truncateLine` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:1224`) is ANSI-aware and already used for banners; `renderDowntimeStatus` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:3077`) returns ANSI-wrapped status strings of varying length.

- No existing tests assert the header's visible length constraint at narrow widths; the overflow only appears visually in the pty and is not caught by current line-count tests which use wide (80/253) cols.

## Desired change

1. In `createListRenderer` list-mode branch (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` ~3220–3233), apply the existing `truncateLine` to the assembled header before pushing it:
   ```ts
   header = truncateLine(header, cols);
   output.push(header);
   ```
   (Keep the existing `output.push` as a single row; do not add a second header row.)

2. Verify the fix maintains the `rows - 1` invariant when the header is long — the header now costs exactly one line regardless of `cols`, so no additional chrome accounting is needed, but the safety clamp at the end of the renderer (`while (output.length > rows - 1) output.pop()`) remains as a backstop.

3. Do not change `renderDowntimeStatus`, `computeDynamicLayout`, `formatDetailView`, or the detail/filter render paths.

4. Update code comments on the header assembly to note the truncation guard and narrow-pane wrap prevention (reference this work item and WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO).

5. Add narrow-pane unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` per AC 4 and ensure all existing tests remain green.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `createListRenderer` list-mode header assembly (`Work Items …` concatenation and `output.push(header)`) and `truncateLine` helper; primary fix location.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Add header truncation and narrow-pane `rows - 1` invariant tests (list mode, with/without banners, varying header lengths); keep existing detail pinned-ToC tests green.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Update if it describes the header/status bar layout; otherwise code-comments only.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO** — "Herdr plugin: selection list header and top lines cut off top of pane" (completed, critical) — introduced the `rows - 1` / `rows` line-count invariant and corrected separator/notification accounting; this item extends the same invariant to the header's own width.
- **WL-0MSI28AP80002F5S** — "Detail view ToC overflows pane — first lines scroll off the top of the screen" (completed) — the detail-view analogue with pinned header+ToC; this list-mode header fix is the list-mode counterpart and must not regress that fix.
- **WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I** — "Detail view ToC for Related Docs" (completed) — introduced the pinned ToC design preserved by the previous item.
- **WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ** — "Herdr selection list: no indication of items below the fold" (completed) — introduced `▲/▼ more` indicators with explicit `budgetForRows - indicatorRows` accounting; relevant to the chrome budget near the header.
- **WL-0MSQ44MDX008U69J** — "Herdr selection list: let list take as much space as it needs; metadata fills the rest and scrolls" (completed) — introduced `computeDynamicLayout` and the `chromeLines = 2 + bannerCount` budget that the header consumes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: Over-truncation hides useful status.** Mitigation: `truncateLine` preserves the leading `Work Items — N item(s)` prefix and only drops trailing status segments; at 40 cols the most informative prefix remains visible and full status is available in wider panes. Document the truncation behavior.
- **Risk: `truncateLine` double-counts ANSI vs display width.** Mitigation: reuse the proven `truncateLine` implementation already used for banners; add a test that asserts visible length (via `stripAnsi`) after truncation, not raw string length.
- **Risk: Growing idle timer (`m:ss`) eventually pushes other segments off.** Mitigation: tested as part of the variable-length `downtimeStatus` combinations; the truncation guard is independent of which status variant is active.
- **Risk: Breaking existing line-count tests that assume header length.** Mitigation: widen the test cols or update expectations to account for truncation — no functional change for 80+ cols where the header already fits.
- **Assumption:** The reported wrap is in **list mode** (the main `Work Items` list), not in detail mode — confirmed by operator (Q4/Q5). If detail-mode header wrapping is later reported, a separate item should cover it.
- **Assumption:** Narrow pane is the primary reproduction (`cols ~ 40–80`); the fix is validated at 40 cols as the lower bound (below 40 the pane is pathological and the existing `while (output.length > rows - 1) output.pop()` backstop applies).
- **Scope creep:** A richer fix could elide individual status segments (e.g. hide `[auto-refresh on]` first, then downtime) instead of raw truncation — explicitly out of scope for this bug; file as a follow-up enhancement if desired.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "When you say 'the info line at the top,' are you referring to the metadata table (Status, Priority, Stage, etc.) that sits below the pinned header in the detail view?" — Answer (user): "I mean the very first line, it contains the Work Items count, the auto-refresh status, the downtime status." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 1, Q1. Research: inspected `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `createListRenderer` header assembly (lines 3217–3229); top line is `Work Items — N item(s) [auto-refresh on] [Downtime …]` plus optional filter/paused segments.
- Q: "Should the fix pin the metadata table as well (so only the description/document viewer scrolls), or is there a different line/section you have in mind?" — Answer (user): "No." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 1, Q2.
- Q: "How many items should be in scope — just the metadata table in the detail view, or also the list-mode metadata panel at the bottom of the pane?" — Answer (user): "It has nothing to do with the meta-data (see 1)." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 1, Q3. Research: confirmed the issue is the list-mode header, not any metadata panel/table; detail view already has a pinned header+ToC via WL-0MSI28AP80002F5S.
- Q: "When this happens, is it the main list header (`Work Items — N item(s)...`) or a different line? And does it happen during normal list mode, or specifically when you're in the detail view for an item?" — Answer (user): "4 main" (i.e. the main list header). Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 2, Q4. Research: `createListRenderer` list-mode branch pushes `header` as `output[0]`; detail-mode path returns via `formatDetailView` and never renders the `Work Items` header.
- Q: "Does it happen with narrow terminal windows (e.g., 80 cols), or also at wider widths?" — Answer (user): "5. Narrow." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 2, Q5. Research: wide pans (253 cols) have ample space for the header; narrow panes (40–80 cols) reproduce the wrap — banners and long filter labels exacerbate it.
- Q: "Does the downtime status text include a timestamp that grows as time passes (e.g., `[downtime idle m:ss]`) — could this growing timestamp eventually cause the header line to wrap?" — Answer (user): "6. no - happens event when it says `[Downtime Off]`." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 2, Q6. Research: `renderDowntimeStatus` (worklist.ts:3077) returns `. [Downtime Off]` (shortest variant) when the worker is disabled — wrap reproduces even with this minimal segment, confirming the bug is not timer-growth-specific; discovered a typo in the answer ("event" = "even") and did not alter the captured intent.

## Summary

`npm run build` in `packages/herdr` exits 2 with 84 `TS6059` errors (`File ... is not under 'rootDir' '/home/.../packages/herdr/src'`).

## Root cause

`packages/herdr/tsconfig.json` sets `rootDir: ./src` and includes `src/**/*.ts`, which includes the `.test.ts` files. Several herdr test files (e.g. `src/implement-tier-blocked-exclusion.test.ts`, worklist tests) import shared CLI test helpers from the repo root (`../../tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts`, `../../src/*`). Those files are pulled into the compilation graph but lie outside `rootDir`, producing TS6059 for every import. tsc still emits the in-root files to `dist/`, but the `cp src/shortcuts.json dist/shortcuts.json` step of the build script never runs (tsc exits non-zero), leaving `dist/shortcuts.json` stale.

## Expected behaviour

- `cd packages/herdr && npm run build` exits 0 and copies `src/shortcuts.json` → `dist/shortcuts.json`.

## Implementation notes

- Exclude test files from the herdr build: add `"exclude": ["**/*.test.ts"]` to `packages/herdr/tsconfig.json` (the test files are compiled/run by vitest, not needed in dist). Verify `npm run build` exits 0 and `dist/` contains no `.test.js` files.
- Check whether `packages/shared/tsconfig.json` has the same pattern (it builds cleanly today — likely no test files there).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cd packages/herdr && npm run build` exits 0.
- [ ] `dist/shortcuts.json` is copied on every build.
- [ ] `npx vitest run packages/herdr` still passes (tests unaffected by the exclude).

Discovered from: WL-0MSNULGSM00018I4

data.description: Sometimes work items get left stuck in in_progress. Every 30 seconds the herdr plugin should retrieve all in_progress work items and attempt to match an active pane to the work item. If none is found then set to either completed, blocked or open. This work item should be blocked on the one to add work item id to pane titles, which can then be used to match panes. All tabs in the current workspace should be searched.
