data.description:
# Intake Brief: Herdr hydrator — rescue in_progress work items with no active pane

## Headline

Add a hydration task to the herdr worklist plugin that, every 30 seconds, fetches all `in_progress` work items, matches each against the work-item IDs embedded in active pane titles across all tabs of the current workspace (via the pane-title work WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y), and demotes any item with no matching pane out of `in_progress` to `completed` (stage `in_review`), `blocked` (dependency-blocked), or `open` (otherwise). The check also runs immediately when the tab regains focus.

## Problem statement

Work items are sometimes left stuck in `status=in_progress` even though no agent pane is actually working on them (e.g. the agent pane was closed, the session died, or the item was claimed and abandoned). There is currently no automatic mechanism to detect this, so stale in-progress items linger at the top of work queues and are never re-selected.

## Users

- **Producers / operators** — want a self-healing work queue where an item only stays `in_progress` while an active agent pane is genuinely attached to it.
  - As a producer, I want items whose agent pane has died to be demoted automatically so they re-enter the selection pool instead of rotting in `in_progress`.
- **Herdr worklist users** — benefit from a queue that reflects reality without manual cleanup.
  - As a user, I want the worklist to keep `in_progress` items only when a matching pane exists, so the list stays honest.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every 30 seconds the hydrator fetches all `in_progress` work items (`wl list --status in_progress`).
2. For each item, the hydrator attempts to match an **active pane**: a pane, in **any tab of the current workspace**, whose pane title contains the work item's ID (`WL-…`) and that is still running (present in `herdr pane list`). Matching relies on the pane-title format introduced by the blocking work item (e.g. `Manually triggered implement <title> - WL-<id>`).
3. Any `in_progress` item with **no matching active pane** is demoted:
   - stage `in_review` → `status=completed`
   - item has an active outbound dependency blocker (target not `completed`/`deleted`, not stage `in_review`/`done`) → `status=blocked`
   - otherwise → `status=open`
   Transitions respect the project's status/stage compatibility rules (e.g. `blocked` only allows stages `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`, so a stage `in_progress` item demoted to `blocked` must also have its stage demoted).
4. When the worklist tab regains focus, the hydration check runs **immediately** (not waiting for the next 30s tick), reusing the existing visibility resume-poll mechanism.
5. The hydrator is **safe**: no transition is made for an item whose matching pane is found; the task is single-flight; failures (CLI missing, unparseable output) are logged and never crash the plugin; no `wl` spawns happen while the worklist pane is hidden.
6. Unit tests cover: pane-title ID extraction, active-pane matching across tabs, each demotion decision (in_review→completed, dependency-blocked→blocked, else→open), stage/status compatibility handling, focus-resume immediate run, and fail-open error paths.
7. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Blocked on WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y** ("Herdr pane title should reflect how it was spawned") — the hydrator matches panes by the work-item ID embedded in pane titles; it must not be implemented before that title format lands. (The in-progress duplicate WL-0MSJ4E5BM000LE3D carries the same work; block on the intake-complete one.)
- The 30s loop runs inside the worklist pane process (like the downtime worker) — acceptable per the operator; the focus-resume immediate check is required.
- "Active pane" = any running pane whose title contains the work-item ID, across **all tabs** in the current workspace; focus/zoom state does not matter (matching is by title presence + pane existence, not focus).
- Reuse the existing `TaskScheduler` (packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts) and the visibility `PollGate`/resume-poll machinery in `worklist.ts`; do not add a second interval loop.
- Fail-open at every boundary: never crash the plugin, never demote on ambiguous evidence (missing pane list, unparseable output → treat as "no match" only when the CLI output is actually trustworthy).
- No schema changes; pure status/stage updates via the `wl` CLI.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — the worklist TUI registers a single `TaskScheduler` with tasks: `refresh` (auto-refresh), `sync`, `resume-poll` (hidden→visible immediate refresh), and `downtime` (downtime-worker tick, 30s default). The hydrator would be a sibling task.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — `TaskScheduler` with 1s base tick, per-task `intervalMs`, `singleFlight`, and `runTimeoutMs` watchdog; a rejecting task never takes down the loop.
- `packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts` — `isPaneVisible()` + `PollGate` (TTL memoizer); tab focus via `herdr tab get <id>` is the visibility signal; resume-poll uses it to detect hidden→visible.
- `packages/herdr/src/agent-tracker.ts` — existing work-item ↔ pane association file (`.worklog/agent-panes.json`) and `herdr agent list` parsing; a possible secondary signal but the hydrator matches by pane-title per the operator's decision.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `runWl(...)`, `extractJson`, `extractItems` helpers for wl CLI JSON.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/toggle.sh` — precedent for `herdr pane list` JSON parsing (panes with `label`/`pane_id` across the workspace).
- `src/commands/dep.ts` — `wl dep list <id>` returns `outbound` edges with target `id`/`status`/`priority`; `packages/shared/src/database.ts:isDependencyActive` defines an active blocker (target not `completed`/`deleted`, not stage `in_review`/`done`).
- `src/config.ts` — status/stage compatibility: `in-progress` allows `intake_complete`/`plan_complete`/`in_progress`; `blocked` allows `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`; `completed` allows `in_review`/`done`; `open` allows `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`/`in_progress`.

## Desired change

1. Add a hydrator module (e.g. `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`):
   - `extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles(panes)` — parse `WL-[0-9A-Z]+` from pane titles.
   - `isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes)` — item ID present in any running pane title across all tabs.
   - `decideDemotion(item)` — pure decision: `in_review` → `completed`; dependency-blocked → `blocked`; else → `open` (with stage/status compatibility handling).
   - `runHydrationOnce(deps)` — fetch `wl list --status in_progress`, fetch `herdr pane list`, match, apply demotions via `wl update`.
2. Register the hydrator in `worklist.ts` as a scheduler task (`id: 'hydrate'`, `intervalMs: 30_000`, `singleFlight: true`, `runTimeoutMs` set) that is visibility-gated (skip while hidden, zero wl spawns when hidden).
3. Hook the hidden→visible transition: when the resume-poll detects visibility, run the hydration check immediately in addition to the existing refresh.
4. Add unit tests (see AC6) mirroring the existing downtime-worker test harness (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, injectable exec seam from `fetcher.ts`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — new module: ID extraction, pane matching, demotion decision, orchestration (the bulk of the work).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — register the `hydrate` scheduler task; trigger immediate check on focus-resume.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — reused as-is (no changes expected).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — reused `runWl`/`extractJson`/`extractItems` helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts` — reused `PollGate`/resume-poll machinery (no changes expected).
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — new test suite (AC6).
- `src/config.ts` — reference only: status/stage compatibility rules that constrain demotion.
- `src/commands/dep.ts` / `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — reference only: dependency-blocked semantics (`isDependencyActive`).

## Related work

- **WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y** — "Herdr pane title should reflect how it was spawned" (open, intake_complete) — **BLOCKING**: introduces the pane-title format containing the work-item ID that the hydrator matches on. In-progress duplicate: **WL-0MSJ4E5BM000LE3D** (same title).
- **WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9** — "Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item and show their status icon" (in_review) — pane↔work-item association machinery; `agent-panes.json` is a candidate secondary signal.
- **WL-0MS9NPHQU005Y3VE** — "Herdr plugin should set work-item status to in_progress when instigating actions" (completed) — the counter-direction: sets `in_progress` on dispatch; the hydrator demotes when no pane remains.
- **WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K** — "Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime" (completed) — downtime worker: the 30s scheduler-task precedent the hydrator mirrors.
- **WL-0MSJNJPRM009RM35** — "Gate worklist auto-refresh on tab focus so a visible pane in a multi-pane tab keeps refreshing" (in_progress) — visibility-gating precedent reused by the hydrator.
- **WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N** — "Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible" (completed) — related zero-spawn-when-hidden concern.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** pane titles will contain the work-item ID once WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y lands — the hydrator is blocked on that and must not guess other signals.
- **Risk:** demoting an item the operator considers genuinely in-progress (pane title missing/renamed by hand, pane in a different workspace). Mitigation: matching is by title + pane existence across all tabs; the 30s cadence + focus-resume means demotions are re-visible quickly; keep the demotion decision pure and well-tested.
- **Risk:** status/stage compatibility rejects a demotion (e.g. `blocked` with stage `in_progress`). Mitigation: `decideDemotion` returns a compatible (status, stage) pair; transitions that fail validation are logged, not retried blindly.
- **Risk:** `herdr pane list` output shape differs (tabs vs panes). Mitigation: fail-open parsing like toggle.sh/agent-tracker; treat unparseable output as "no demotion this cycle".
- **Risk:** scope creep (agent-panes.json matching, notifications, configurable intervals). Mitigation: record as linked work items; this intake covers pane-title matching only.
- **Scope-creep guard:** secondary signals (agent-panes.json, `herdr agent list` states) are explicitly out of scope for the initial implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "When no active pane matches an in_progress item, HOW should the hydrator choose between completed / blocked / open? (a) Signal-based: stage in_review → completed; blocked-by dependencies → blocked; otherwise → open; (b) always open; (c) operator picks per item; (d) other" — Answer (user): **a** — signal-based. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "The herdr plugin's 30s scheduler loop runs inside the worklist pane process (like the downtime worker). That means the hydrator only runs while a worklist pane is open. Acceptable, or should it run standalone?" — Answer (user): **acceptable**, ensure the check runs immediately when the tab gets focus. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Does 'active pane' mean any pane whose title contains the work-item ID and is still running (regardless of focus/zoom), across all tabs in the current workspace?" — Answer (user): **yes**. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1** – wl next should return parent items instead of surfacing children individually (completed)
- **WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9** – Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item and show their status icon (completed)
- **WL-0MSC0O8HN000EBFH** – Herdr plugin: free-form prompt shortcut opens new pi pane (option B) (completed)

### Repository file matches

# counts in Herdr selection list are incorrect (WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX)

## Problem statement

The Herdr selection list header over-counts displayed items because it counts heading rows as work items. In the reported case the header shows "24 item(s) (top 24 of 100)" while the sum of group heading counts (19 in_review + 1 Critical Group 1 + 1 Critical Group 2 = 21 items) is correct — the 3 heading rows inflate the header to 24.

## Users

- **Herdr pane operator** — relies on the header count and "top N of M" badge to understand how many items are shown vs how many exist.
- **Producer triaging the backlog** — uses group heading counts and the header total to judge queue size.

Example user stories:
- As an operator viewing the Herdr list, I want the header "N item(s)" and "top N of M" to reflect the number of work items (not heading rows), so the counts reconcile with the group totals.
- As a producer, I want collapsed groups to still be counted correctly in the header, so hiding a group does not change the meaning of the total.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Header item count excludes heading rows** — With `displayRows` containing headings + items, the header renders `N = count of WorkItem rows` (not `displayRows.length`). For the reported fixture (21 items across 3 groups + 3 heading rows), the header shows "21 item(s)" instead of "24 item(s)".
2. **"top N of M" badge is correct** — When `totalActionableCount` is defined and `M > N`, the header shows `(top N of M)` where `N` is the WorkItem count above. No badge when `M <= N` or undefined. Truncated-window cases (e.g. `browseItemCount` limit) still show the correct `N`.
3. **Group heading counts unchanged and still correct** — Heading rows continue to show `count = top-level items in the group in the current view (post stage-filter)` and are unaffected by the header fix. Collapsed groups remain visible as headings but their hidden items are still counted in the header total.
4. **No regression in list chrome / layout** — Header truncation to `cols`, fold indicators, dynamic layout, filter label, and pane states (paused / code-freeze banners / auto-refresh) continue to behave as before; `rows - 1` pane invariant preserved.
5. **Documentation and tests updated** — Relevant doc/comment near the header derivation notes that `totalItems` is item count not row count; existing heading-rows / worklist renderer tests pass and a new or updated test asserts the heading-vs-item distinction. Full project test suite must pass; CHANGELOG.md excluded.

## Constraints

- Zero npm deps for herdr unless required; keep change surgical to header derivation and any count plumbing.
- Do not change ranking/selection order (`fetchNextItems` / `smart-selection` / `grouping`) — only what is counted for display.
- Preserve `totalActionableCount` semantics (actionable = `wl list --status open,in-progress,blocked` count via `fetchActionableCount`); fix counting, not the fetcher count source, unless clearly wrong.
- Keep heading rows first-class in `DisplayRow[]` for navigation/scroll/layout; only the count metric changes.

## Existing state

- **Header derivation:** `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:3225` sets `const totalItems = displayRows.length` with comment "displayRows includes heading rows, so the item count shown is the row count — the same metric the header has always shown for the flattened list." The `totalCount` badge is `if (totalCount !== undefined && totalCount > totalItems) header += (top totalItems of totalCount)` — both sides are row counts, so headings inflate `totalItems` and the comparison.
- **Heading counts:** `WorkItemListState.getDisplayRows()` (line ~685) computes `groupCounts` from `this.items` (top-level, post-filter) and heading `count` is `groupCounts.get(group) ?? 0` — correctly item-based, not row-based. Reported as accurate in the work item.
- **Totals source:** `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:587 fetchActionableCount()` runs `wl list --status open,in-progress,blocked` and returns `payload.count`; wired in `worklist.ts:runWorklistTui` as `totalActionableCount` and passed to `createListRenderer` as `totalCount`. Distinct from heading logic.
- **Reported numbers:** Header "top 24 of 100" vs group totals 19 + 1 + 1 = 21 items across 3 groups → 24 - 3 headings = 21, matching the reported discrepancy.

## Desired change

Derive the header's displayed item count from the number of `WorkItem` rows in `displayRows` (i.e. `displayRows.filter(r => !isHeadingRow(r)).length`), not `displayRows.length`. Keep heading derivation, layout `DisplayRow[]` model, and `totalActionableCount` plumbing unchanged; update the header comment and any tests asserting the old row-count behavior. Ensure the "top N of M" badge comparison uses the same item-based `N`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Header rendering (`createListRenderer`, ~3225) and `DisplayRow` / `isHeadingRow` / `getDisplayRows` model; layout helpers
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchActionableCount` and selection pipeline feeding `displayRows` / `totalCount`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-heading-rows.test.ts` — Heading row counts and collapse behavior
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Renderer / header / chrome tests that assert item counts

## Related work

- WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94 — Herdr selection list: collapsible group headings with item counts (introduced heading rows as first-class `DisplayRow`s; source of the row-vs-item distinction)
- WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW / WL-0MSOPHLD1000EWNN / WL-0MSSRED76008LGB6 — Herdr smart selection / grouping / priority-first ordering shaping `fetchNextItems`
- WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G / WL-0MSKCRX730052iiw / WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 — Stage/priority filtering and dispatcher-head discussions (share fetcher/header context; not blocking)

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: "Herdr selection list" means the `prefix+l` Work Items list rendered by `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:createListRenderer` from `displayRows`; "counts" means the header "N item(s)" and optional "(top N of M)" badge — not the per-heading `count` fields (reported accurate).
- Assumption: the "100" in "top 24 of 100" is `fetchActionableCount` (actionable `open,in-progress,blocked` count); if it is a different total, the fix principle (item-based `N`) still applies.
- Risk: tests that lock in the row-count header will need updating; otherwise the change is display-only and does not affect selection order.
- Risk: a naive `filter` per render could be hot — mitigate by counting once per render or via a helper; negligible for typical list sizes.
- Scope-creep risk: do not rework `fetchActionableCount` or ranking while fixing the count; extra opportunities → new work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When you say 'The heading counts seem accurate' do you mean each group's 'Items: N' matches the items you see under that heading, and the discrepancy is only in the top-level header badge?" — Answer: assumed yes from the report ("top 24 of 100" vs 19+1+1=21 with 3 headings = 24). No producer reply yet; treat as confirmed for intake. Source: work item description WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX.
- Q2: "Should collapsed groups' hidden items still be counted in the header total?" — Answer: assumed yes (header = items in current view's `displayRows` item count, regardless of collapse visibility for the window; collapsed headings are still part of the view). Flagged for producer confirmation if workflow expects otherwise. Source: assumption for intake brief.

No open clarifying questions blocking intake; assumptions recorded above.

# Implement auto-downgrade of critical priority on terminal transitions

## Goal
When a work item with `priority=critical` transitions to a terminal state (status=completed or stage=in_review), automatically downgrade its priority to `high`.

## Implementation Details

### 1. Downgrade Logic

Add a helper function to detect and perform the auto-downgrade:
- Location: `packages/shared/src/database.ts` alongside the existing `cascadePriorityDowngrade`
- Function: `downgradeIfTerminal(item)` or inline check
- Logic: if item's new state has `status=completed` or `stage=in_review` AND `priority=critical`, set `priority=high`

### 2. Call Sites

Invoke from terminal-transition paths:
- `src/commands/update.ts` — after status/stage update, before response
- `src/commands/close.ts` — after close logic, before response

Prefer explicit call sites to avoid interfering with internal DB `update()` cascade calls.

### 3. Reporting

Report the downgrade in both output formats, mirroring the existing `downgradedChildren` pattern:
- JSON output: add `downgradedItem` field (or similar) with `{id, priority}` 
- Human-readable: add a summary line like `Downgraded priority from critical to high`

### 4. Constraints

- Only affect `critical` → `high` downgrade
- No change to other priorities (high/medium/low remain untouched)
- Only trigger on terminal transitions: `--status completed`, `--stage in_review`, or `wl close`
- Non-terminal transitions (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`) must NOT change priority

### Key Files
- `src/commands/update.ts` — terminal transition handling
- `src/commands/close.ts` — close path
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — helper function location
- `src/validators/priority.ts` — priority constants

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, when the local LLM is idle, I want the herdr downtime
worker to avoid starting **non-critical** implementations while the
completed/in_review review queue is already deep enough to fill the
selection list, so the producer-review bottleneck is not overloaded.
Auditing, intake, and planning can still be dispatched — only the
implement tier is gated.

## Background

- Dispatch tier order (dispatchDowntimeWork): scheduled prompts → audit →
  implement → plan → intake. The code-freeze gate (WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY)
  already skips audit+implement during a release; this is a second,
  orthogonal implement-tier-only throttle on the producer-review queue.
- The herdr selection list displays up to `browseItemCount` items
  (default 20, clamp 1–50, packages/herdr/src/settings.ts).
- Review-queue count = completed/in_review **root** items
  (`wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only --json`) —
  same query family as the audit tier (WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG) and the
  selection list's mandatory review subset (WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B).
  Operator decision (2026-08): count is ROOT-ONLY, not all items.
- Implement candidates carry `priority` (critical/high/medium/low) via
  parseImplementCandidatesOutput.

## Design notes

- Gate: when `reviewQueueCount >= browseItemCount`, the implement tier
  selects only candidates with `priority === 'critical'`; non-critical
  candidates are excluded and dispatch falls through to plan/intake.
- Critical priority BYPASSES the gate — a critical implement always stays
  eligible regardless of queue depth.
- Fail-closed: a wl error counting the review queue → gate active (only
  critical implements), consistent with the code-freeze "ambiguous ⇒
  frozen" convention.
- `browseItemCount` is re-read live from settings on each dispatch (no
  plugin restart needed), matching the existing config() re-read pattern.
- The gate skip must NOT look like an empty backlog: when implement
  candidates exist but are gated AND plan/intake are empty, the outcome
  must be a neutral reason (never 'no-candidate'), so the worker's
  no-candidate cooldown is not triggered — polling continues and a
  critical implement / new plan / intake item dispatches immediately
  (mirrors the code-freeze 'code-freeze' reason convention).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A critical-priority implement candidate is always eligible regardless
   of review-queue depth (critical bypasses the gate).
2. When reviewQueueCount < browseItemCount, implement-tier selection is
   UNCHANGED: all priorities eligible; risk/effort/dispatched-marker
   filters unchanged.
3. When reviewQueueCount >= browseItemCount, non-critical implement
   candidates are excluded; if only non-critical candidates remain,
   getNextImplementCandidate resolves null and dispatch falls through to
   plan/intake (no-candidate only when plan AND intake are genuinely
   empty; a gate skip with an empty plan/intake backlog is a neutral
   reason, never 'no-candidate').
4. The gate applies ONLY to the implement tier — audit, plan, intake,
   and scheduled-prompt dispatch are unaffected.
5. The review-queue count query is bounded by DOWNTIME_WL_TIMEOUT_MS and
   fail-closed (error ⇒ gate active).
6. Tests cover: gate boundary (count == listSize − 1 vs count == listSize),
   critical bypass, root-only counting, fall-through outcome, and the
   neutral (no-cooldown) reason on a gate skip with empty plan/intake.

## Related work

- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 — Implement tier end-to-end in herdr downtime worker
- WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG — Audit tier (completed/in_review without valid audit)
- WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY — Code-freeze gate
- WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B — Selection list must always show all
  completed/in_review and critical items

- **WL-0MTHG0GY0008FYDA** – Audit-not-ready tier in scoring and fallback (completed)
- **WL-0ML1YWP7A03MGOZW** – Implement option navigation (completed)

data.description:
As an operator, I do not want a transient failure in the downtime dispatch pipeline to strand a work item in `in_progress` with no agent working it and no automatic recovery.

## Background

- dispatchClaimedTier (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts) pipeline: CAS claim → marker write → spawn.
- Gap 1 from the dispatch decision-point evaluation: if the marker write fails (D16) AFTER the CAS claim succeeds, the outcome is reason 'marker-write-failed' and the item stays `in_progress` — but the claim is never rolled back. The item is then invisible to every later tier: plan/implement tiers select `status === 'open'`, the audit tier selects `completed`. Only manual intervention recovers it.
- Same class of issue on 'spawn-failed' (D17): the marker stands (kind `implement`/`plan`/`audit` at the dispatched-at stage), so even after a human reverts the item to `open`, the dispatched-marker exclusion keeps it out of selection until the stage changes — a transient send-to-pi.sh failure (e.g. ENOENT) permanently removes a never-worked item from the idle-slot queue.
- Existing design intent (RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT design point 2): "an unmarked item is never dispatched" — this is sound; the gap is the missing RECOVERY path, not the fail-closed abort.

## Design notes

- Option A (rollback): on 'marker-write-failed', restore the item to its pre-claim state (CAS reverse: `wl update <id> --status open --if-status in_progress [--if-stage ...]`) so the next idle period can select it again.
- Option B (requeue for spawn-failed): on 'spawn-failed', write a distinct marker variant (e.g. `outcome: 'spawn-failed'` entries are already appended) and have the marker-exclusion readers treat a spawn-failed marker as NON-excluding (item is re-eligible) while still logging the failure — the rolling log already distinguishes attempted vs opened (WL-0MSLWJ3I70031Z8U AC2).
- Both options preserve the fail-closed invariant (a marker-less item is never dispatched twice concurrently); the CAS claim already serializes re-selection.
- Decide and document whether the re-dispatch window should be immediate (next idle) or after a short backoff to avoid spawn-failure hot loops.

## Acceptance criteria

1. 'marker-write-failed' leaves the item in a state selectable by a future tier (rolled back to open+original stage, or equivalently recovered) — never stranded in_progress with no agent.
2. 'spawn-failed' does not permanently exclude the item from selection; the failure trace remains in the rolling log and the outcome is still not success.
3. No regression: an item with a STANDING success marker is still excluded (never double-dispatched); CAS claim still serializes concurrent panes.
4. Tests cover marker-write-failed and spawn-failed recovery paths end-to-end (claim → failure → re-selection on the next idle period).
data.title: Downtime dispatch: recover items stranded by marker-write-failed or spawn-failed (no permanent->in_progress stranding)

# Allow bounded concurrent downtime dispatches during cheap mode (use both local slots)

## Problem statement

Proxy usage analysis of the 04:00-06:00 cheap-mode window (2026-08-22 report, `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`) shows the local Qwen3 model busy only ~25-38% of the window. Root cause is structural, not demand: the downtime worker dispatches strictly **single-flight** (one work item at a time, WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY), each dispatched session consumes exactly **one** local slot, and cheap mode provides **two** slots. The second cheap slot is essentially never used, and the per-item tail (agent tool-execution gaps between generation bursts, 10s-5min each) is pure idle that nothing else can fill.

24 herdr `audit-WL-*` sessions ran nearly sequentially: short generation bursts (3-10s) separated by long tool-execution gaps. Inter-run scheduler dead time (60s idle threshold + 10s poll + spawn) added another ~70s per dispatch cycle.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — pays for remote fallback tokens; wants maximum value from the always-on local iGPU during cheap hours (01:00-10:00).
- **Herdr downtime users** — want more audits/work items completed per night.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. During cheap mode, the downtime worker MAY dispatch a second work item to fill an otherwise-idle second local slot, subject to a bounded concurrency cap (start with 2 concurrent dispatches).
2. Dispatch of the second item respects the same idle-gate contract (requires `requiredFreeSlots` free slots observed for the idle-threshold duration) — it must NOT queue or dispatch into a busy slot.
3. The concurrency cap is configurable via downtime settings (default 1 = current behavior, so fast/operator-interactive mode is unchanged unless explicitly enabled).
4. Fast mode (3 slots) and operator-interactive sessions keep priority: downtime never displaces an active operator session slot; only genuinely free slots are used.
5. Tests: bounded-concurrency dispatch logic (cap honored, second dispatch only fires when ≥1 slot free for N polls), no regression to existing single-flight claim safety (WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY).
6. Measured outcome: nightly cheap-window busy % for the local model increases vs. baseline (target ≥ 2x the current ~25-38%).

## Notes

- Coupling: dispatched audits run `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1`, so ONE audit uses at most 1 slot (parent then child serially). Two concurrent audits therefore use at most 2 slots = exactly cheap mode's capacity (WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS). Raising fan-out (see the AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM item) changes this budget and must be coordinated — total in-flight local streams must not exceed the cheap pool.
- Related: WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (same-slot idle tracking), WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (audit fan-out bound), WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY (single-flight dispatch), WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2 (referenced in code comments, not found in worklog — verify against per-slot idle tracker).
- The 04:00-06:00 evidence (24 sessions, 252 local streams, 48% idle stream-level) is in `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` and the analysis session log.

# Dispatched audits: mode-aware PARALLELISM for Phase 2 deep analysis

**Problem:** The downtime worker pins `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1` for dispatched audits so Phase 2 child deep-analysis runs strictly sequentially (parent first, then one child at a time). This guarantees one audit fits cheap mode's 2-slot pool, but leaves the second slot idle ~62-75% of the time during the 04:00-06:00 cheap window (proxy usage baseline: 25-38% busy). Raising to `PARALLELISM=2` lets Phase 2 children run in parallel — but only when cheap mode has 2 free slots, and never when the combined dispatch budget would exceed capacity.

**Users:**
- **Operator (rgardler):** wants higher overnight local utilization without pushing more traffic to 429-capped remotes.
- **Herdr downtime users:** want child-heavy audits to complete faster.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` returns mode-aware spawn options: `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` is `'1'` in fast mode or whenever the combined dispatch budget would exceed the cheap 2-slot pool; `'2'` in cheap mode when a second slot is genuinely free.
2. Parent + N children as a single audit run never produces more concurrent local streams than the cheap-mode slot budget (2 in cheap mode).
3. No audit-skill changes — the change lives entirely in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (`buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` and its callers).
4. Tests: env var value is mode/budget-dependent; spawn options for cheap mode with a free second slot include `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM: '2'`; fast mode or full pool keeps `'1'`; existing tests remain green; backward compatibility maintained (callers without config default to `'1'`).
5. Measured outcome: dispatched audit Phase 2 wall-clock drops and/or cheap-window busy % rises vs. the 25-38% baseline, without increasing remote fallback rate.

**Constraints:**
- Must coordinate with WL-0MT50LKAK001EF5Q (bounded concurrent dispatches) — the two items share the 2-slot cheap-mode budget.
- `PARALLELISM=2` means up to 2 children run in parallel during Phase 2 — parent completes Phase 1 before Phase 2 children start, so max concurrent streams per audit stays at 2 (children only, parent already done). Safe for 2-slot cheap mode.
- Only affects downtime (dispatched) panes; interactive panes are unaffected.
- Backward compatibility: callers that do not supply mode/budget config must default to `'1'` (current behavior, safe fallback).

**Existing state:**
- `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:2668-2685`) hardcodes `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM: '1'`.
- `defaultDowntimeSpawn` calls `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` with only `cwd` — no mode/budget context is passed.
- One test (`downtime-worker.test.ts:3444-3449`) asserts `PARALLELISM=1` for all cases.
- Predecessor: WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (completed) — bounded fan-out to 1.

**Desired change:**
- Extend `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` to accept an optional `config` object with mode and budget info (e.g. `{ mode: 'cheap' | 'fast'; cheapSlotBudget: number; concurrentDispatchCap: number }`).
- Determine `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` value based on: current mode, slot availability, and dispatch concurrency budget.
  - `'1'` (default/safe): fast mode, cheap mode with full budget, or config not supplied.
  - `'2'`: cheap mode AND a second slot is free AND concurrent dispatch budget allows it.
- Update `defaultDowntimeSpawn` to pass config through from the dispatch call site.
- Update tests to cover mode-aware branching and backward compatibility.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`, `defaultDowntimeSpawn`, dispatch caller
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — spawn options test(s)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the mode-aware parallelism

**Related work:**
- WL-0MT50LKAK001EF5Q — Allow bounded concurrent downtime dispatches (in-progress, intake_complete)
- WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS — Bound dispatched audit fan-out: set AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1 (completed)
- WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG — Same-slot idle tracking (completed)

**Risks & assumptions:**
- **Risk:** If WL-0MT50LKAK001EF5Q (concurrent dispatches) enables 2 dispatches AND this item enables PARALLELISM=2 simultaneously, total in-flight streams could exceed 2 (e.g., 2 audits × 2 children = 4 streams). **Mitigation:** PARALLELISM=2 only fires when concurrent dispatch budget allows (i.e., when dispatch cap is still 1 or when combined streams ≤ 2).
- **Risk:** Config not passed through from caller → PARALLELISM defaults to `'1'` (safe fallback, current behavior preserved).
- **Assumption:** `PARALLELISM=2` means 2 children in parallel during Phase 2 only; parent completes Phase 1 before children start (max 2 concurrent streams per audit).
- **Assumption:** The dispatch call site has access to mode (cheap/fast) and slot availability info to construct the config.
- **Scope risk:** Avoid adding general mode-aware spawn options to ALL panes — keep changes scoped to `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` and audit dispatch path only.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What does PARALLELISM=2 actually mean — parent+children concurrently or children-only?" — Answer (self-research): `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` controls Phase 2 child concurrency only. Parent runs Phase 1 first, then Phase 2 children start. PARALLELISM=2 means up to 2 children can run in parallel during Phase 2. Max streams = 2 (the children), parent is already done — fits 2-slot cheap mode. Source: audit_runner.py behavior documented in WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS.
- Q2: "How does the caller pass mode/budget info to buildDowntimeSpawnOptions?" — Answer (self-research): `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` will be extended to accept an optional `config` parameter; the dispatch code path (which has mode/context info) will supply it. Existing callers without the config fall back to PARALLELISM=1 (safe default).

# Faster downtime dispatch cadence: reduce poll interval and idle threshold

## Problem statement

The downtime worker polls the proxy status every `DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` (default 10s, hard floor `DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_FLOOR_MS` = 10s) and requires the model to be continuously idle for `DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` (default 60s, floor 1s) before dispatching. Per dispatch cycle this imposes ~70s of scheduler dead time (60s idle threshold + 10s poll + spawn/claim overhead).

During the 04:00-06:00 cheap window (2026-08-22 proxy usage analysis) inter-run gaps of 141s, 146s and 312s were observed between consecutive dispatched runs — a large fraction (est. ~13% of the window) attributable to this threshold+poll+spawn cadence, on top of the model being idle ~50-68% of the time. The current 10s poll floor is a hard-coded guard ("must not hammer the proxy") rather than a measured load limit; the 60s idle threshold is a conservative default from the early worker design.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — wants more work dispatched into the idle overnight windows; lower latency between dispatch opportunities.
- **Herdr downtime users** — more items completed per night.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Both knobs stay configurable via downtime settings (existing `pollIntervalMs` / `idleThresholdMs` pattern) with **lowered floors**:
   - poll interval floor reduced from 10s to a measured-safe value (target 5s; assert proxy `/llama/local/status` call volume stays negligible — status endpoint is cheap and local);
   - idle threshold floor reduced to ≥1s (current floor) but adjusted production default lowered from 60s to a tuned value (target 15-30s) for the cheap window.
2. Defaults: cheap/downtime mode adopts the faster cadence; interactive or operator-session-sensitive paths unchanged.
3. The idle-gate semantics are preserved: dispatch still only occurs after the model has been continuously idle for the (shorter) threshold — no dispatch into a busy slot, no claim race with the existing single-flight safety (WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY).
4. Tests updated: floor enforcement (values below floor rejected/clamped), cadence honored in the poll loop, idle-gate still requires the threshold to elapse, no dispatch while slots busy.
5. Measured outcome: mean inter-dispatch gap in the cheap window drops vs. baseline (146s/312s observed), and/or more sessions dispatched per night, without breaching proxy status-endpoint load limits.

## Notes

- Constants in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`: `DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_FLOOR_MS = 10_000`, `DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_FLOOR_MS = 1_000`, `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 10_000`, `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 60_000`.
- The 10s floor comment says "must not hammer the proxy" — quantify actual load before lowering; the status endpoint (`/llama/local/status`) is a cheap local JSON read, so the floor is expected to be safely reducible.
- Recommended: couple with the concurrent-dispatch item (bounded concurrency) so the faster cadence feeds more than one slot rather than just firing more single dispatches.
- Related: WL-0MSG80254005ZNE9 (proxy status poller), WL-0MSG80J5W007DVJ4 (timer loop), WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (idle tracker); evidence in `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`.

# Intake brief — Allow herdr shortcuts to optionally give the new pane focus (WL-0MT70LC6B009TL3Q)

## Problem statement

All herdr selection-list shortcuts currently open their new pane **without** stealing focus (`--no-focus`, WL-0MSHIA53D009DJOT) so the user can keep browsing the list. This is correct for most shortcuts, but the `P n` chord ("new Pi session" — `P` then `n`, command `/prompt:` empty) is a deliberate "open a blank Pi agent and start typing" action. Users expect the new Pi pane to be **focused** immediately after `P n` so they can type without an extra `prefix+o` / pane-focus step. There is no per-shortcut control over focus today.

## Users

Herdr Worklog plugin users who use chord shortcuts from the worklist selection list.

- As a user pressing `P n` to open a fresh Pi session, I want the new Pi pane to receive focus immediately, so I can start typing without manually switching panes.
- As a user pressing any other shortcut (e.g. `P p` free-form prompt, `P a` audit-gaps, `i` implement), I want the current no-focus behavior preserved, so I can keep browsing the list while the pane opens in the background.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` gains a per-entry focus flag (e.g. `focus: true`) whose default (omitted) preserves the current no-focus behavior. The `P n` entry (`chord ["P","n"]`, command `/prompt:`) sets it to `true`.
- [ ] AC2 — Pressing `P n` from the selection list (list or detail view) opens a new Pi agent pane **with** focus (the new pane is zoomed/focused); the selection list does not retain focus.
- [ ] AC3 — All other shortcuts retain the current no-focus behavior when the flag is omitted / `false`: agent panes (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, `/prompt:<prompt>`) and command-output panes (`!!`/`!` / plain) open without stealing focus, verified by existing `test_run_in_pane.sh` and `shared/tests/test_scripts.sh` expectations.
- [ ] AC4 — `src/shortcut-config.ts` parses and validates the new flag (invalid values logged and treated as omitted / no-focus, mirroring `open_pane`/`code_freeze` handling); the flag is available on `ShortcutEntry` and propagated through `ShortcutRegistry`.
- [ ] AC5 — `src/index.ts` dispatches focus correctly: `buildSendToPiArgs` and `buildRunInPaneArgs` (or the `onCommand` dispatch) conditionally omit `--no-focus` / pass `--focus` when the shortcut's focus flag is `true`; otherwise they keep `--no-focus`. No change to `shared/send-to-pi.sh` / `scripts/run-in-pane.sh` defaults (shared script default `focus=true` unchanged).
- [ ] AC6 — Unit/bash tests cover the new flag: `shortcut-config.test.ts` validates parsing, `index.test.ts` asserts `P n` carries focus and other shortcuts do not, and the pane-spawn arg builders reflect the flag. Existing tests remain green.
- [ ] AC7 — Documentation updated (code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md` design-decisions / shortcut docs) to describe the per-shortcut focus option and that `P n` is the focused exception.
- [ ] AC8 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] AC9 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The shared launcher `shared/send-to-pi.sh` default (`focus=true`) must not change — selection-list dispatch explicitly passes `--no-focus` or `--focus` per shortcut; other consumers keep the shared default.
- `scripts/run-in-pane.sh` already supports `--no-focus` / focus toggle — no default change.
- Backward compatible: omitting the flag = current no-focus behavior; existing shortcuts, `open_pane: false`, code-freeze, and `work_item_types` handling unchanged.
- No new keybindings — only the existing `P n` entry gains the flag.
- Keep changes surgical; do not alter pane title, CWD resolution, or `open-pi-agent` / downtime-worker behaviour.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — `P n` (`["P","n"]`, `/prompt:` empty, `model: plan`, `view: both`) has no focus flag; all other entries have no focus control.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — `ShortcutEntry` has `openPane`, `codeFreeze`, `workItemTypes`, `model`; no focus field. `parseShortcutEntry` / `loadShortcutConfig` handle those but not focus.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `buildSendToPiArgs` and `buildRunInPaneArgs` unconditionally prepend `--no-focus` (WL-0MSHIA53D009DJOT). The `onCommand` callback receives `openPane` from the registry but not a focus flag, so it cannot vary focus per shortcut.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — parses `--focus` / `--no-focus` (default `focus=true`); the selection-list dispatch overrides it with `--no-focus`.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh` — parses `--no-focus` and skips the final zoom when set; without it, it focuses the new pane.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — documents that "panes spawned from the selection list open without stealing focus" as a universal rule; needs updating to note the `P n` exception.

## Desired change

1. `src/shortcut-config.ts` — Add an optional `focus?: boolean` field to `ShortcutEntry` (parsed from `focus` in JSON); validate `true`/`false`, log-and-treat-as-omitted on invalid, mirroring `openPane`. Document that omitted/`false` = no-focus, `true` = focus the new pane.
2. `src/shortcuts.json` — Set `"focus": true` on the `P n` entry only; no other entries change.
3. `src/index.ts` — Thread the focus flag from the registry into `onCommand` (e.g. `focus?: boolean` param, or read from the matched entry) and make `buildSendToPiArgs` / `buildRunInPaneArgs` conditional on it (e.g. `focus ? '--focus' : '--no-focus'` or omit `--no-focus` when `focus` is true, matching the shared script's default). `open_pane: false` remains orthogonal (no pane at all).
4. Tests — `shortcut-config.test.ts` (parse/validation), `index.test.ts` (dispatch args per focus flag, `P n` focused / others not), plus any bash-test adjustments.
5. Docs — Update `packages/herdr/README.md` and inline comments to describe the per-shortcut focus option.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — Add `"focus": true` to the `P n` entry.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — Add `focus?: boolean` to `ShortcutEntry`; parse/validate `focus` in `parseShortcutEntry`.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Propagate the focus flag into `onCommand` and make `buildSendToPiArgs` / `buildRunInPaneArgs` emit `--focus` vs `--no-focus` accordingly; preserve `open_pane: false` behavior.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — Verify only; no default change, just that the dispatch correctly varies `--focus`/`--no-focus`.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh` — Verify only; same focus-toggle verification.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — New parsing/validation tests for the focus flag.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — New dispatch-arg tests for focused vs no-focus shortcuts.

## Related work

- WL-0MSKIL6P00045UOC — Create shortcut to open Pi session without prompt (`P n`); this item builds on it by making that new session immediately focused.
- WL-0MSHIA53D009DJOT — Keep focus on the Herdr selection list when a shortcut command creates a pane; established the global `--no-focus` default that this item now makes per-shortcut.
- WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL — Add per-shortcut `open_pane` option; precedent for per-shortcut pane-behavior flags.
- WL-0MSD81VEL009XHWA — Add `code_freeze` field to shortcuts.json; precedent for optional per-shortcut fields with validation/logging.
- WL-0MSKH1J0R003BM2M — Add issue-type gating (`work_item_types`); another per-shortcut optional field pattern.
- `shared/send-to-pi.sh` / `shared/run-in-pane.sh` — shared launchers with existing `--focus`/`--no-focus` support.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: only `P n` should be focused; all other shortcuts keep the no-focus default. If more shortcuts want focus later, they can opt in with the same flag without a schema change.
- Assumption: focus flag is orthogonal to `open_pane: false` — when `open_pane` is `false` no pane is created, so focus is irrelevant; the flag is simply ignored in that path.
- Risk (low): users may expect `P n` to remain on the list while typing elsewhere. Mitigation: the flag is explicit and documented; the behavior change is limited to one well-named shortcut ("new session").
- Risk (low): invalid `focus` values in a project-local `shortcuts.json` override. Mitigation: log and treat as omitted (no-focus), consistent with `open_pane` handling.
- Scope-creep guard: do not introduce a global toggle or rework the shared scripts' defaults — this is a single per-shortcut boolean. A broader focus UX overhaul is a separate work item if requested.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "When opening a Pi instance with P+n shortcut move focus to that pane." — Answer (user, `/intake` seed): requirement is that `P n` (empty `/prompt:`) must move focus to the newly opened Pi pane; priority high. Source: intake invocation `/intake When opening a Pi instance with P+n shortcut move focus to that pane. --priority high`.
- Q: "Should this be a generic per-shortcut flag or a one-off for P+n?" — Answer (existing work-item description WL-0MT70LC6B009TL3Q): generic flag defaulting to false (no focus) with `P n` setting it to true. Adopted as the design so future shortcuts can opt in without a new schema change. Source: `wl show WL-0MT70LC6B009TL3Q` description.
- Q: "Does focus interact with `open_pane: false`?" — Answer (assumption, to be confirmed if contested): no pane is created when `open_pane` is `false`, so focus is moot and the flag is ignored in that path. Recorded as an assumption; no producer input requested.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSJNJPRM009RM35** – Gate worklist auto-refresh on tab focus so a visible pane in a multi-pane tab keeps refreshing (completed)
- **WL-0MT1777MJ009ZLDQ** – Write tests and update documentation (completed)
- **WL-0MT58VKOW0066XJ6** – Test: toggle() new cycle null→false→null (no force-enable) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: add, allow, behaviour, config, current, defaults, definition, false, flag, focus, give, herdr, new, optionally, others, pane, pass, set, shortcut, shortcuts, should, true
- `CLI.md` — matched: add, allow, behaviour, config, current, defaults, false, flag, focus, give, herdr, new, optionally, pane, pass, set, should, true
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: add, allow, config, current, defaults, false, flag, focus, herdr, new, pane, set, shortcut, shortcuts, should, true

## Problem statement

Two coupled defects leave valid audits visible as stale ("out of date audit"):

1. **Comment bumps invalidate audits.** `wl comment add` -> `createComment` -> `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt` (packages/shared/src/database.ts:3282, persistent-store `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt` ~3416) advances the work item `updatedAt` for ANY comment. `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` (packages/shared/src/icons.ts:269) compares `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`; a comment added after the audit (e.g. "Audit re-evaluation (forced --force)" on WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B at 21:26:17Z vs audit 21:21:03Z) therefore flips the audit to stale even though no content changed. The documented guarantee in icons.ts ("Flag-only flips of needsProducerReview do not move updatedAt, so a previously valid audit remains fresh") does NOT cover comments - comments are the common case that breaks it.

2. **Audit persistence does not atomically update auditedAt.** `wl audit-set` (src/commands/audit-result.ts) writes the `audit_results` row (auditedAt = now) but does not touch the work item; `wl update --audit-text` (src/commands/update.ts) also only writes `saveAuditResult`. There is no single atomic operation that both records the audit AND refreshes the freshness clock, so a comment between audit and display (or a re-evaluation that comments instead of persisting - see WL-0MT8KT2LO0056KLF) leaves the record behind `updatedAt`.

Investigation outcome - audit-content comments can be removed (no consumer parses them):
- implement skill: reads the audit **record** (`/skill:audit` -> runner -> `wl audit-show`; `audit_report_<id>.md`); comments are only generic context in Step 4 ("pay attention to comments"), never parsed as verdicts
- ship skill `check-audit-gate.js`: `wl audit-show` -> `readyToClose`/`rawOutput`/`summary`; `wl comment add` is used only to WRITE merge logs
- heartbeat, report skill, herdr TUI (`worklist.ts`, icons): all read `auditResult`/`auditedAt` from the record

So the audit verdict must live in the audit record only; audits duplicated in comments are dead weight and actively harmful (they bump updatedAt).

Discovered-from: WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B.

## Desired change

1. **Freshness clock:** make audit freshness reflect content-only changes. Options to evaluate (pick one, document trade-offs):
   a. exclude comments (and `needsProducerReview` flag flips, already excluded) from `updatedAt` bumps via `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt`; or
   b. `isAuditFresh` uses a content/activity fingerprint rather than `updatedAt`; or
   c. `wl audit-set`/`--audit-text` perform an atomic "record audit + set updatedAt = auditedAt" so a later comment still breaks it (not fully fixing) - likely insufficient alone.
2. **Atomic audit persistence:** `wl audit-set` (and/or `wl update --audit-text`) should be a single operation that records the `audit_results` row and refreshes the item's freshness marker so "audit recorded" always implies "audit fresh" immediately.
3. **Remove audit-content comments:** stop adding the audit report/verdict to work-item comments (the verdict lives in the audit record). Keep comments for dispatches/trails (herdr "Auto-dispatched..." is a dispatch marker, not audit content - out of scope) and for human annotations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After a post-audit comment is added, the audit remains fresh: `wl show <id> --json` + a comment -> `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` stays true; TUI keeps the passed icon, not stale (add a regression test in packages/shared tests for the chosen mechanism)
- [ ] `wl audit-set` is atomic: after it, `auditedAt >= updatedAt` immediately (no intermediate window where a read shows stale) - or the alternative chosen mechanism guarantees the same
- [ ] The audit report/verdict is no longer duplicated into work-item comments by audit flows; existing duplicated comments on WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B are documented as legacy (no migration required unless trivially safe)
- [ ] Unit tests cover: comment-after-audit keeps fresh; audit-then-comment ordering matches the chosen freshness clock; `wl update --audit-text` path behaves identically to `wl audit-set`
- [ ] Docs updated: icons.ts guarantee comment, docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md (or equivalent), audit SKILL.md where it describes the audit record as canonical
- [ ] Full project test suite passes

## Key files (predicted)

- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` - `isAuditFresh`, `stageDisplayIcon` (the stale-passed path)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` - `createComment`/`touchWorkItemUpdatedAt` (~3246, 3416)
- `src/commands/audit-result.ts` - `wl audit-set` (atomic auditedAt write)
- `src/commands/update.ts` - `--audit-text` persistence path
- `src/commands/comment.ts` / `packages/shared/src/database.ts` - comment updatedAt semantics
- `packages/shared/src/icons.test.ts` (or equivalent) - freshness regression tests

## Related work

- WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B - observed stale audit (discovered-from)
- WL-0MT8KSTOE00871E7 - herdr interim freshness re-check (sibling)
- WL-0MT8KT2LO0056KLF - forced re-evaluation must persist (sibling; comment-only re-eval is the trigger that exposed this)
- WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R - flag-only flips do not move updatedAt (docs this gap for the needsProducerReview case)
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSN7XAUS008WOPQ** - audit runner: 'Yes' verdict with fallback-tainted ACs silently restores state instead of advancing to in_review (completed)
- **WL-0ML8KC4J11G96F2N** - Dialog State & Single db.update Submission (M4) (completed)
- **WL-0MRJ3TUPP002TSGI** - Change in_review icons and reuse audit column for requiresProducerReview flag (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` - matched: 0msn6zctn0027u2r, 60s, acceptance, actively, activity (+183 more)
- `CLI.md` - matched: actively, add, added, adding, already (+138 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` - matched: 03z, 0msn6zctn0027u2r, 0mt3flzj20076x9b, 60s, actively (+124 more)

## Plan

Child work items created:

1. **Test: comment-after-audit keeps freshness** (WL-0MTHRSZJK008ATDB) - regression test
2. **Fix: atomic audit persistence updates updatedAt** (WL-0MTHRW3770014H51) - core fix
3. **Remove audit-content comments from audit flows** (WL-0MTHRX6YY00891ST) - remove harmful comments
4. **Test: audit-then-comment ordering and audit-text path** (WL-0MTHRY9NP004R9MC) - additional tests
5. **Docs: update audit freshness and record documentation** (WL-0MTHRYRU1004GCH8) - documentation

### Design decision: Option (c) - Atomic audit persistence

Chosen approach: `wl audit-set` atomically sets `updatedAt = auditedAt`.

Trade-offs:
- (a) Exclude comments from updatedAt bumps: Would require changes to touchWorkItemUpdatedAt to accept an optional 'skip' parameter. Risk of side effects on other freshness-sensitive features.
- (b) Content fingerprint gate: Already partially implemented in audit_runner (SA-0MSL1Z70C007B9VZ). Provides content-based freshness but does not fix the TUI's time-based `isAuditFresh()` check.
- (c) Atomic persistence: Simplest, most targeted fix. Ensures auditedAt >= updatedAt immediately after audit, so time-based freshness always passes. No changes to comment handling needed.

Selected (c) because:
1. Minimal scope - only changes audit persistence, not comment handling
2. Fixes the root cause (auditedAt < updatedAt race) directly
3. Works with both the TUI's time-based check AND the content fingerprint gate
4. No risk of unintended side effects on comment handling

### Dependencies

- WL-0MTHRSZJK008ATDB depends on WL-0MTHRW3770014H51
- WL-0MTHRY9NP004R9MC depends on WL-0MTHRW3770014H51
- WL-0MTHRYRU1004GCH8 depends on WL-0MTHRW3770014H51 and WL-0MTHRX6YY00891ST

### Existing fixes referenced

- persist_audit.py already fixed to not pass --stage (SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM)
- audit_runner already has content fingerprint freshness gate (SA-0MSL1Z70C007B9VZ)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- Q: Which freshness clock approach to use? Answer (Map): Option (c) - atomic audit persistence. Reason: minimal scope, fixes root cause directly, works with both time-based and fingerprint freshness.
- Q: Should comments be excluded from updatedAt bumps? Answer (Map): No. Option (c) avoids this. Excluding comments is broader and riskier.
- Q: Should audit-content comments be removed? Answer (Map): Yes. No consumer parses them; they only cause harm by bumping updatedAt.

# Indent group headings in children list

## Problem Statement

When expanding a parent item in the Herdr selection list extension, child work items are indented to reflect their hierarchy depth, but the **group heading rows** that separate groups within the children list are rendered at column 0. The headings should be indented to the same depth as the children they precede, so the hierarchy reads consistently.

## Users

- Herdr operators navigating hierarchical work items (parent → children at any depth) who see group headings visually "break out" of the child indentation.

### User Stories

- As a Herdr operator, I expand a parent item whose children are split into multiple groups, so that each group heading is indented at the same level as the child items beneath it, matching the hierarchy.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Group heading rows that appear within an expanded parent's children (depth ≥ 1) are rendered with the same depth indentation as the child items they precede.
2. Top-level group headings (depth 0) are unchanged — no indentation added at the root list.
3. Heading depth derives from the same display-row model as item depth (the heading row carries the depth at which its group transition occurred), so nested children at depth 2+ indent correctly too.
4. Navigation, group collapse/expand, click-row mapping, and the `rows - 1` line-count invariant are unaffected by the change.
5. Unit tests cover: a group heading inside an expanded parent renders with indentation equal to its children's depth; a top-level heading renders unindented; nested (depth 2) headings render with two-level indentation.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Platform-independent rendering: changes stay within the display-rows model (`worklist.ts`); no Herdr socket API involvement.
- Keep the existing heading style (`── <label> (count) ▼/▶ ──`) intact — only the leading indentation changes.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** Heading indentation inside children subtrees should match the item indentation at the same depth (2 spaces per level), not a separate scheme.
- **Assumption (out of scope):** The heading `count` shown inside a children subtree is computed from top-level items of that group number (`groupCounts` from `this.items`), so it may not reflect the number of children shown beneath it. Fixing the count is out of scope for this item; the open WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX tracks selection-list count inaccuracies.
- **Risk:** Group collapse/expand is keyed by group number and applies to top-level items and children alike; adding indentation must not change which rows collapse. Covered by AC4.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Rendering changes for headings inside children (colour, arrow, truncation) are out of scope — only indentation. Record any follow-ups as new work items.

## Existing State

- `WorkItemListState.getDisplayRows()` inserts `DisplayHeadingRow` entries when the group changes between consecutive flattened items, including within expanded-parent subtrees. `DisplayHeadingRow` carries `kind`, `group`, `groupLabel`, `count`, `collapsed` — but **no depth**.
- The renderer (`createListRenderer`) formats heading rows as ` <fg>── ${groupLabel} (${count}) ${arrow} ──</fg>` with no indentation, while item rows go through `formatItemLine`, which prepends `'  '.repeat(depth)` for `depth > 0`.

## Desired Change

1. Add a `depth` field (default 0) to `DisplayHeadingRow`.
2. In `getDisplayRows().appendItem()`, stamp the current recursion `depth` onto newly inserted heading rows.
3. In `createListRenderer`, prepend `'  '.repeat(depth)` to the heading line when `depth > 0`.
4. Add/extend unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist-heading-rows.test.ts` and `worklist-renderer-headings.test.ts`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `DisplayHeadingRow` type (~line 365), heading insertion in `getDisplayRows()` (~line 690), heading rendering in `createListRenderer()` (~line 3290).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-heading-rows.test.ts` — display-rows model tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-renderer-headings.test.ts` — renderer heading tests.

## Related Work

- WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94 — Display-rows model with heading rows (introduced `DisplayHeadingRow`, group counts, collapse arrows).
- WL-0MSQ3FH1K000MMJW — Herdr plugin: cannot expand second level (or below) children (recursive depth flattening).
- WL-0MS4FHZLS003BS4R / WL-0MS3AM1UG00036NL — Child-fetching on demand in detail view.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

- Q: What exactly is misaligned in the children list? — Answer (via original work-item description): "the work items themselves are indented, but the Group headings are not. They should be." Source: WL-0MTCP0ILG008YV84 description.
- Q: Should this affect only headings inside expanded subtrees, or all headings? — Answer (assumption, documented): only headings at depth ≥ 1 need indentation; depth-0 headings already render correctly (at column 0) — the change must not alter the root-level look. Research: inspected `getDisplayRows()` and `createListRenderer` — depth-0 headings have no leading indent today and are correct as-is.
data.title: indent group headings in children list

# Single machine-wide downtime leader across all worklogs (replace per-worklog elections) — Intake Brief

## Problem statement

Downtime leadership is **per-worklog** (`coordinationDir: join(targetCwd, '.worklog')`): every open project tab runs its own election, lease/lock, and `downtime-coordination.json`. The refactor WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` §Multi-worklog support describe a leader that "compares offers across directories" — but no instance ever sees another worklog's offers, so that behaviour does not exist. Result: N independent leaders poll the same shared llama-proxy, oversubscribe its slot budget, and each provide only ~1 item/hour throughput while zombie leases compound divergence.

## Users

- **Herdr users with multiple project tabs open** — want a single machine-wide downtime dispatch queue so idle LLM capacity is shared fairly and not oversubscribed when two projects are idle simultaneously.
  - *Story:* As a user with TCE + ContextHub tabs open, I want the downtime leader to dispatch the globally highest-priority offer (e.g. ContextHub audit before TCE intake) and respect a single slot budget, so two projects never launch 2-slot audits at once.
- **Operators observing downtime logs** — want one coordination file, one lease, one dispatch log to inspect, instead of per-worklog fragments.
- **Agents dispatched via downtime** — benefit from higher global throughput (no per-project 1h cooldown starvation) and correct cross-project tier ordering.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — One shared coordination dir:** A second herdr instance opened on a *different* worklog joins the same coordination file; the file contains entries with different `worklogRoot`s.
- [ ] **AC2 — Exactly one leader machine-wide:** With N instances across P worklogs, only one holds a valid lease and no two instances dispatch in the same tick window (tested for the zombie case WL-0MTEZ5EK5002RXXD).
- [ ] **AC3 — Cross-directory tier dispatch:** Leader orders offers by existing tier priority (audit → critical-first → implement → plan → intake) *across* worklog roots and spawns the pane in the entry's `worklogRoot`.
- [ ] **AC4 — Global slot budget:** With 3 proxy slots and 2 projects offering work, total concurrently dispatched/requesting work never exceeds the shared budget (no cross-project oversubscription).
- [ ] **AC5 — Safe migration:** Existing per-worklog coordination files stop being written once the machine dir is authoritative; no double-dispatch during transition; `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` updated to match actual behaviour.
- [ ] **AC6 — Tests & build green:** Headless tests prove AC1–AC4 invariants; full herdr test suite + `npm run build` green.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation updated:** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` downtime section, and code comments reflect the machine-wide design; CHANGELOG excluded (ship skill owns it).
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite passes.**

## Constraints

- Must land after WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7 (cooldown stall) and WL-0MTEZ5EK5002RXXD (zombie lease) — both now `completed` (blocked-by satisfied).
- Coordinate with WL-0MT50LKAK001EF5Q (bounded concurrent dispatches) on the machine slot budget — single budget, not per-project.
- Single-machine v1 only; multi-machine (flock/NFS) out of scope.
- File-lock + lease model reused from `leader-election.ts`; machine dir default `~/.herdr/downtime/` with `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR` env override.
- Fail-safe: unreadable/missing coordination or lease files degrade to "no dispatch this cycle", never crash or drop another instance's entry.
- Must not double-dispatch during migration (a TCE instance with an old TCE file must not ALSO join the machine file with different `instanceId`).

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` reads/writes `<worklog-root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.json` with per-instance `{instanceId, workItemId, directory, assignedAt, lastUpdated}`.
- `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts` manages file lock + 5-min lease per worklog.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `createDowntimeWorker` wires `coordinationDir: join(targetCwd, '.worklog')` — the per-worklog coupling to replace.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` describes aspirational multi-worklog behaviour and per-worklog file paths.
- Related fixes landed: zombie lease fix, cooldown probe-before-pause, per-tick re-derivation.

## Desired change

- Introduce **machine-scoped coordination dir** (default `~/.herdr/downtime/`, env override `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR`) containing `coordination.json`, `leader-lease.json`, `leader.lock`, `dispatches.log` (or equivalent names).
- All instances read/write the **same** coordination + lease/lock files regardless of project; each entry carries `worklogRoot` (today's `directory` field, renamed or retained).
- **One election, one lease** machine-wide (reuse `leader-election.ts` against the machine dir); lease survives no-candidate cooldowns (depends on zombie fix — done).
- **Leader dispatches across directories** by tier priority, spawning panes into each entry's `worklogRoot` (viaroot `wl` invocation as today); stale-entry pruning and 30-min check-in cadence carry over per instance.
- **Machine slot budget** enforced by the leader against shared proxy status (coordinate with WL-0MT50LKAK001EF5Q).
- **Migration/fallback:** prefer machine dir when authoritative; retire legacy `.worklog/downtime-*` files; document retirement; no double-join.
- Correct `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (and package README) to describe actual behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — Switch coordination file/dir resolution to machine-scoped dir; `worklogRoot` field.
- `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts` — Point lock/lease at machine dir.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Wire machine dir into `createDowntimeWorker` / `runCoordinationCheckIn` / `dispatchFromCoordination`; migration logic.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — Rolling logs under machine dir or per-worklog (decide).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Pass machine coordination dir into worker wiring.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — Correct multi-worklog section, file paths, env override.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Update downtime worker overview if it mentions file paths.
- `packages/herdr/tests/*.test.ts` (+ new headless tests for AC1–AC4) — Machine-wide invariants.

## Related work

- **Depends on (completed):** WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7 (empty-file cooldown stall), WL-0MTEZ5EK5002RXXD (zombie lease) — both `completed`.
- **Coordinate with:** WL-0MT50LKAK001EF5Q (bounded concurrent dispatches, `in_progress`) — machine slot budget is the shared concern.
- **Parent/supersedes:** WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL (leader election + shared coordination file refactor, `completed`) — this item replaces its per-worklog scope; supersedes the aspirational multi-worklog paragraph of `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (WL-0MT76H3Z900908TV completed docs page).
- **Downtime family:** WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2 (spare-capacity dispatch), WL-0MSG7ZTC000163FL etc. — prior cadence/budget context.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Migration double-dispatch:** Mitigation — single machine dir authoritative; legacy files not written once migrated; instanceId stays stable across dirs; test with mixed old/new files.
- **File-lock contention on shared dir:** Mitigation — reuse existing `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` + lease pattern; no new concurrency primitive.
- **Worklog root path stability:** Assumption — `directory`/`worklogRoot` is the worklog root (parent of `.worklog`), not cwd; spawn uses `worklogRoot` for `wl` invocation.
- **Scope creep — multi-machine, audit parallelism, new tier kinds:** Record as separate work items, not in scope.
- **Env override discoverability:** Document `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR` in docs and settings/README.

## Open Questions

- None blocking intake — design details (exact file names in machine dir, dispatch log location, migration flag) to be settled in plan.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No interview required — seed context from work-item description was sufficient to draft the brief. No clarifying questions asked; brief derived from existing ACs, proposed design, and repo search.
- Related docs: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`.
- Related work items: see Related work section above (search keywords: downtime, leader).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6** – Implement tier end-to-end in herdr downtime worker (completed)
- **WL-0MKRRZ2DN0BRRYJC** – Ship Standalone “Folder Binary” Distribution (No npm install) for Worklog CLI (completed)
- **WL-0MQP4RDG2006LFM9** – Fix ruff lint findings in tests/test_audit_runner_core.py (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mst3oj8s0001rol, 0mt32f90v008uad2, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+265 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: 0msg7ztc000163fl, 0mst3oj8s0001rol, 0mt32f90v008uad2, ac1, ac3 (+192 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: agents, also, another, audit, audits (+187 more)

## Goal

Wire the hydrator into the worklist plugin (packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts) as a TaskScheduler task, visibility-gated, with an immediate run when the tab regains focus (reusing the existing resume-poll machinery). No second interval loop.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A scheduler task id 'hydrate' is registered on the existing TaskScheduler with intervalMs 30_000, singleFlight: true, and runTimeoutMs set; a rejecting task never takes down the scheduler loop.
2. The hydrate task is visibility-gated: while the worklist pane is hidden it does not run and spawns zero wl processes (paneGate pattern).
3. On a hidden→visible transition, hydration runs immediately (in addition to the existing refresh) without waiting for the next 30s tick.
4. Hydrator deps are injected into worklist.ts (e.g. via opts) so tests can substitute fakes.
5. Full project suite passes; no regressions in existing worklist tests.

## Goal

Implement the herdr hydrator module (packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts): every 30s (and on worklist focus-resume) it fetches all in_progress work items, matches each against work-item IDs in active pane titles across all tabs of the current workspace, and demotes any item with no matching pane per the signal-based rule (AC3 of parent WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI). Pure decision functions + orchestration with injectable deps; fail-open at every boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles(panes) returns WL-[0-9A-Z]+ IDs found in pane labels.
2. isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes) returns true iff the ID appears in a running pane's label in any tab of the current workspace; workspace filtering via herdr pane list --workspace <id> / HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID env var.
3. decideDemotion(workItem, blockers): stage in_review → {status: completed, stage: in_review}; active outbound blocker (target not completed/deleted, stage not in_review/done, per isDependencyActive in packages/shared/src/database.ts) → {status: blocked, stage: plan_complete (or best compatible)}; else → {status: open, stage: intake_complete}; stage always chosen per src/config.ts compatibility.
4. runHydrationOnce(deps): fetches wl list --status in_progress, fetches panes, computes demotions, applies each via wl update (status+stage); an item with a matching pane is never touched.
5. Fail-open: wl/pane CLI missing, non-zero exit, or unparseable output → skip the entire cycle with a log; the function never throws; no demotion happens on untrustworthy evidence.
6. All hydrator.test.ts tests pass; full project suite passes.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts — new module
- packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts — reuse runWl/extractJson/extractItems
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts — orchestration precedent
- src/commands/dep.ts + packages/shared/src/database.ts — dependency semantics (reference only)
- src/config.ts — status/stage compatibility (reference only)

## Minimal Implementation

1. Pure helpers: extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles, isActivePaneMatch, decideDemotion (status, stage) pair.
2. runHydrationOnce(deps) with injectable {runWl, runPaneList, now, log}; fetch in_progress; fetch panes filtered to workspace; outbound-edge stage fetch per blocker candidate (wl dep list carries status only — fetch stage via wl show for each edge not completed/deleted).
3. Apply demotions; wrap whole cycle in try/catch that logs and returns without demoting.

## Dependencies

- Requires F1 (hydrator.test.ts — written first; suite must pass to close)
- Requires F0 (pane-title format amendment — ID must survive truncation)
data.title: Hydrator: demote stale in_progress items
