# Intake Brief — Replace binary author-identity gate with configurable author whitelist (WL-0MTGDW58X007UJDS)

## Problem Statement

`wl sync` currently uses a binary author-identity gate (`syncAllowForeignAuthor` boolean): it either allows only commits from the local `user.email` or allows all foreign authors. This causes false-positive refusals for single operators with multiple emails/machines and does not scale for team or CI scenarios that need a selective allow-list.

## Users

- **Single operator, multiple machines/emails** — wants sync to succeed when their own secondary email appears on the remote without opening the gate to everyone.
- **Team lead / shared repo** — wants to allow a known set of collaborators' emails while still rejecting unknown authors.
- **CI / automation** — wants to allow a bot email in addition to the human operator without disabling the gate entirely.

### Example User Stories

- As a developer with `sorra@thewizardscode.com` on laptop and `alice@company.com` on CI, I want to whitelist both emails in `.worklog/worklog.yaml` so `wl sync` merges remote commits from either without requiring `--allow-foreign-author` on every run.
- As a project maintainer, I want the default (`syncAllowedAuthors: []`) to preserve the strictest behavior (only local `user.email`) so existing single-author repos see no security regression.
- As an operator who previously used `syncAllowForeignAuthor: true` or `--allow-foreign-author`, I want that flag to keep working (mapped to allow-all) so I am not broken by the migration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Config schema:** `syncAllowedAuthors` is accepted in `.worklog/config.yaml` / `config.defaults.yaml` with validation: `[]` (empty list, default), non-empty string list, `null`, or `true` (allow-all). Invalid types are rejected with a clear error.
- [ ] **AC2 — Gate behavior:** Empty list enforces current behavior (only local `user.email` accepted); non-empty list accepts any email in the whitelist; `null`/`true` allows any author (equivalent to current `--allow-foreign-author`). Empty-author commits are always refused regardless of whitelist.
- [ ] **AC3 — CLI compatibility:** `wl sync --allow-foreign-author` still works and overrides the config to allow-all for that invocation; help text (`wl sync --help`) explains the whitelist model (`[]` default, list, `null`/`true` allow-all) and the flag's override semantics. Existing `--allow-foreign-author` users are unaffected.
- [ ] **AC4 — Tests:** Automated tests cover: empty-list strict gating, non-empty whitelist allows listed / rejects unlisted, `null`/`true` allows all, empty-email always refused, and CLI flag override. Existing sync author-gate tests continue to pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — Docs & suite:** Help text and relevant docs (e.g. `SYNC_IDENTITY_GATE.md` / `CONFIG.md` or equivalent) describe the whitelist model. All related documentation and code comments are updated. Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Default `[]` must preserve current security posture — no widening of the gate for existing repos without explicit config change.
- Empty author email is never bypassed (neither whitelist nor `--allow-foreign-author` nor `null`/`true` allows it).
- Backward compatibility: `syncAllowForeignAuthor` boolean and `--allow-foreign-author` flag must keep working; migration should not break existing users. Prefer whitelist as canonical, boolean as deprecated alias or mapped value.
- Email comparison should be case-insensitive (or documented as case-sensitive if intentionally strict) — assumption: case-insensitive, trimmed comparison.
- Minimal scope: config + gate logic + CLI flag wiring + help/docs + tests. No changes to merge logic beyond the gate.

## Existing State

- Author-identity gate lives in `src/sync.ts` (`checkAuthorIdentity`, `enforceAuthorIdentityGate`, `getConfiguredUserEmail`, `getRemoteAuthorCommits`) and is wired in `src/commands/sync.ts` via `getSyncDefaults` / `performSync` → `enforceAuthorIdentityGate`.
- Config key `syncAllowForeignAuthor?: boolean` is defined in `packages/shared/src/types.ts` and consumed in `src/commands/sync.ts` (`getSyncDefaults`). No `syncAllowedAuthors` exists yet.
- `src/config.ts` loads/merges `config.defaults.yaml` + `config.yaml` and validates statuses/stages; no whitelist validation.
- Related work: WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB (identity gate), WL-0MSUEO62N0019P3S (checkAuthorIdentity), WL-0MSUEOAQO0081TJH (wire gate + flag + sync-point), WL-0MTGH78A4000ZVNB (refusal verbosity/exit).

## Desired Change

- Add `syncAllowedAuthors?: string[] | null | true` to `WorklogConfig` (canonical whitelist). Keep `syncAllowForeignAuthor` as deprecated alias that maps to `null` (allow-all) when `syncAllowedAuthors` is unset, or document precedence.
- Add `syncAllowedAuthors: []` (or commented example) to `config.defaults.yaml` (test fixture defaults) and update validation in `src/config.ts` to accept `[]`, `string[]`, `null`, `true`.
- Replace binary gate in `src/sync.ts` (`checkAuthorIdentity` / `enforceAuthorIdentityGate`) to read the whitelist from config: `[]` → only `user.email`; non-empty → `user.email` plus listed emails; `null`/`true` → allow all (except empty-email).
- Update `src/commands/sync.ts` `getSyncDefaults` and CLI registration so `--allow-foreign-author` overrides to allow-all (and optionally `--sync-allowed-authors` or equivalent if desired; at minimum flag → allow-all). Update help text to explain whitelist model.
- Update docs (`SYNC_IDENTITY_GATE.md` and/or `CONFIG.md` / `DATA_SYNCING.md`) and add tests covering AC4.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` — Add `syncAllowedAuthors?: string[] | null | boolean` to `WorklogConfig`; keep `syncAllowForeignAuthor` as deprecated alias
- `src/config.ts` — Validate/normalize `syncAllowedAuthors` (allow `[]`, `string[]`, `null`, `true`); merge with defaults
- `src/sync.ts` — Modify `AuthorIdentityOptions` / `checkAuthorIdentity` / `enforceAuthorIdentityGate` to enforce whitelist instead of pure boolean
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — Wire `syncAllowedAuthors` via `getSyncDefaults`; keep `--allow-foreign-author` as allow-all override; update help text
- `src/sync-defaults.ts` / `.worklog/config.defaults.yaml` (test fixture) — Add default `syncAllowedAuthors: []` and/or documentation
- `docs/sync/SYNC_IDENTITY_GATE.md` (or `CONFIG.md` / `DATA_SYNCING.md`) — Document whitelist model
- `tests/sync-author-gate.test.ts` / `tests/cli/sync-author-gate.test.ts` — Add whitelist coverage

## Related Work

- **WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB** — Sync: identity gate — refuse merge of foreign/empty-author commits (completed) — parent feature this refines
- **WL-0MSUEO62N0019P3S** — Implement checkAuthorIdentity gate in src/sync.ts (completed)
- **WL-0MSUEOAQO0081TJH** — Wire identity gate into wl sync + config flag + sync-point persistence (completed)
- **WL-0MTGH78A4000ZVNB** — Author-identity gate refusal must surface at default verbosity and exit non-zero (completed)
- **WL-0MTGH7ALW002BOQN** — Recovery path for already-diverged worklog repos (completed)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk — Ambiguous precedence:** Both `syncAllowForeignAuthor` and `syncAllowedAuthors` could be set. Mitigation: define clear precedence (whitelist wins when set; boolean is deprecated alias / maps to `null` only when whitelist absent); document and test.
- **Risk — Email normalization:** Case/whitespace differences could cause false refusals. Mitigation: trim + case-insensitive comparison; document.
- **Risk — Scope creep:** Temptation to add regex/wildcard matching or per-branch whitelists. Mitigation: out of scope; record as follow-up work items if requested.
- **Assumption — `null` and `true` are equivalent allow-all** per proposed solution; `undefined`/absent means default `[]`.
- **Assumption — Empty-email gate remains unconditional** (never bypassed).
- **Assumption — No new CLI flag for the list needed in v1**; whitelist is config-only, CLI flag remains allow-all override. A `--sync-allowed-authors` flag can be a follow-up.

## Appendix — Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should `syncAllowForeignAuthor: true` be deprecated or kept indefinitely?" — Answer: Keep for backward compatibility; treat as alias that maps to `syncAllowedAuthors: null` when whitelist is unset. Precedence: explicit `syncAllowedAuthors` wins. Source: Proposed solution AC + existing-state analysis; no producer input yet — recorded as assumption.
- Q: "Should email comparison be case-insensitive?" — Answer: Assumed case-insensitive trimmed comparison (common for emails). Alternative (case-sensitive) would cause surprising refusals; document choice. Source: assumption, to be confirmed if producer prefers strict matching.
- Q: "Is a CLI flag to set the whitelist needed (e.g. `--sync-allowed-authors a@x,b@y`)?" — Answer: Not required for v1; whitelist is config-only, `--allow-foreign-author` covers the allow-all escape hatch. CLI list flag can be a follow-up if requested. Source: scope constraint, inferred from proposed solution.

## Related Docs

- `src/sync.ts`
- `src/commands/sync.ts`
- `src/config.ts`
- `packages/shared/src/types.ts`
- `src/sync-defaults.ts`
- `docs/sync/SYNC_IDENTITY_GATE.md`
- `tests/sync-author-gate.test.ts`

Potentially related docs: `CONFIG.md`, `DATA_SYNCING.md`

## Goal

Regression test confirming that adding a comment after an audit does NOT invalidate the audit in the TUI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Test asserts isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt) returns true when updatedAt was advanced by a comment added after auditedAt
- [ ] Test simulates the race: audit then comment then freshness check
- [ ] Test is in packages/shared/src/icons.test.ts (or equivalent)
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new test

## Implementation notes

This test verifies the chosen freshness clock mechanism. The test must:
1. Create a work item
2. Set an audit (simulating wl audit-set)
3. Add a comment (simulating wl comment add)
4. Assert isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt) is still true

The mechanism must be one of:
- (a) Comments excluded from updatedAt bumps
- (b) Content fingerprint gate
- (c) wl audit-set atomically sets updatedAt = auditedAt
data.title: Test: comment-after-audit keeps freshness

## Goal

Fix the freshness clock so that post-audit comments do not invalidate audits.

## Problem

`wl comment add` calls `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt()` which updates `updatedAt`.
The `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` check in icons.ts returns false when
`auditedAt <= updatedAt - 60s`, so a comment added after the audit makes it
appear stale.

## Proposed solution

Option (c) - atomic audit persistence: `wl audit-set` (and `wl update --audit-text`)
should atomically set `updatedAt = auditedAt` (or `updatedAt >= auditedAt`) when
recording an audit. This ensures that immediately after an audit, the freshness
check always passes, regardless of subsequent comments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl audit-set` sets updatedAt = auditedAt (or later) atomically with the audit record
- [ ] `wl update --audit-text` path behaves identically
- [ ] After audit, `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` returns true immediately
- [ ] No race window where a read between audit-set and display sees stale data

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` - `saveAuditResult` method
- `src/commands/audit-result.ts` - `wl audit-set` command
- `src/commands/update.ts` - `wl update --audit-text` command
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` - `isAuditFresh` function
data.title: Fix: atomic audit persistence updates updatedAt

## Goal

Stop audit flows from duplicating audit results into work-item comments.

## Problem

The `audit_pr.py` `append_audit_comment()` function writes the full audit
result as a comment on the work item. This is redundant because:

- The audit verdict lives in the audit record (audit_results table)
- The implement skill reads the audit record, not comments
- The ship skill reads the audit record
- The heartbeat and TUI read the audit record

The comment is actively harmful: it calls `wl comment add` which bumps
`updatedAt`, potentially invalidating audit freshness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `audit_pr.py` `append_audit_comment()` is removed or disabled (dry_run only)
- [ ] No audit flow adds the full audit report/verdict to work-item comments
- [ ] Dispatch markers ("Auto-dispatched...") and human annotations are preserved
- [ ] Existing duplicated comments on WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B are documented as legacy

## Key Files

- `audit_pr.py` - `append_audit_comment()` function
- Audit runner scripts that call `append_audit_comment`

# Sprint Complete: Auto-Disable Dispatch & Ship Banner

## Problem statement

When all work items in the current sprint have been completed or reviewed (i.e., completed/in_review count >= the browseItemCount setting), the herdr extension should automatically disable downtime dispatching and display a green banner prompting the operator to ship.

## Users

- **Sprint lead / operator**: Sees a clear visual signal when the sprint is done and knows they can ship.
- **Downtime worker**: Stops wasting compute resources dispatching work when there's nothing left to do.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Auto-disable dispatch**: When `completed + in_review` item count >= `browseItemCount` setting, the downtime worker automatically disables dispatching (writes the disable marker, same mechanism as the `d` shortcut).
2. **Green sprint-complete banner**: A green-background, white-text banner replaces the help text below the item list displaying: `Sprint Complete, hit S to ship`.
3. **Re-enable on new items**: When new work items arrive (completed/in_review count drops below `browseItemCount`), the disable marker is removed and the banner disappears, restoring normal behavior.
4. **Banner only when sprint complete**: The sprint-complete banner is shown ONLY when the condition is met AND the help text is enabled (`showHelpText: true`); it does not interfere with code-freeze banners.
5. **All tests pass**: Full project test suite passes with new changes.
6. **Related documentation updated**: Code comments and any relevant docs reflect the new behavior.

## Constraints

- **Fail-closed**: If the item count query fails, default to NOT auto-disabling (conservative).
- **Non-blocking**: The auto-disable must not crash the TUI or block normal operation.
- **Marker reuse**: Use the existing `.herdr-downtime-disabled` marker file mechanism — no new persistence mechanism.
- **Banner placement**: Banner replaces the help text footer area (same chrome row budget accounting as code-freeze banners).

## Existing state

- The `browseItemCount` setting (default 20) controls how many items are displayed.
- The downtime worker already has a disable-marker mechanism (`.herdr-downtime-disabled`) used by the `d` shortcut.
- Code-freeze banners already render above the item list with proper chrome row accounting.
- The help text footer is rendered below the list and is gated by `showHelpText`.
- Completed/in_review items are tracked via `wl list --status completed --stage in_review`.

## Desired change

- Add a completion-check hook that runs on each list refresh and worker tick.
- When the completion condition is met: write the disable marker, suppress the help text footer, and render the green banner.
- When the condition clears: remove the disable marker, restore the help text, and remove the banner.
- The banner text includes "hit S to ship" referencing the existing `S` shortcut for ship confirmation (WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Add completion check logic to the worker tick loop; wire auto-disable into the existing marker mechanism.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Add `sprintComplete` boolean parameter to the renderer; render green banner in place of help text when active.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-disable-marker.ts` — Reuse existing marker write/remove functions; add a `sprintCompleteMarkerExists` check if needed.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — Add `fetchCompletedItemCount()` helper to count completed/in_review items.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — No changes needed (uses existing `browseItemCount`).

## Related work

- Code-freeze banners: `WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY` — similar banner rendering pattern.
- Disable marker: `WL-0MT4BWUHW008LIFE` — existing `.herdr-downtime-disabled` mechanism.
- Ship confirmation dialog: `WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY` — the `S` shortcut the banner references.
data.title: Auto-disable dispatching when sprint is complete

# Intake Draft — Downtime dispatcher: exclude items needing producer review from selection

**Work item:** WL-0MTIAL65N004T22F

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime dispatcher auto-dispatches the next eligible work item during idle LLM slots, but it currently ignores the `needsProducerReview` flag. Items flagged `needsProducerReview=true` are awaiting a human producer decision and should not be auto-worked; dispatching them wastes local slots, conflicts with the review gate, and can trigger work the producer explicitly paused.

## Users

- **Herdr operators** running `packages/herdr` downtime dispatch in local-model idle periods.
- **Producers** who set `needsProducerReview` to gate an item until human review completes.

User stories:
- "As an operator, I want downtime dispatch to skip items awaiting producer review so idle slots are spent on actionable work."
- "As a producer, I want flagging an item for review to immediately remove it from the downtime queue so it is not auto-started while I review it."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Downtime dispatch never selects an item with `needsProducerReview === true` as a candidate, across every tier: audit (`completed`/`in_review` without valid audit), implement (`plan_complete` with risk/effort caps), critical-first (critical across stages, including frontier blockers), `intake_complete` → `/skill:plan`, and `idea` → `/skill:intake`. Items with `needsProducerReview === false` or absent/undefined remain dispatchable.
- AC2: The critical-frontier resolver also excludes `needsProducerReview=true` blockers: if the highest-priority critical candidate is blocked only by review-gated blockers (or the critical item itself needs review), the tier returns no candidate and falls through to the next tier.
- AC3: Coordination (leader) path is equally gated: the leader's per-entry fetch/classification (`fetchItem` + tier mapping) skips entries whose current item has `needsProducerReview === true`; the offer list retains the entry for later re-offer after the flag is cleared, and dispatch falls through to the next dispatchable entry.
- AC4: Filtering is fail-safe at every boundary: a missing/unparseable `needsProducerReview` field is treated as `false` (dispatchable); a malformed item never crashes dispatch and never disables a tier.
- AC5: Regression tests cover the exclusion per tier (unit + `downtime-worker`/`index` level) and verify that clearing the flag makes the item dispatchable again; existing herdr and project test suites pass.
- AC6: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- AC7: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Change is confined to the dispatch selection path; do not change the meaning of `needsProducerReview` elsewhere (TUI filters, `wl list --needs-producer-review`, status lifecycle remain unchanged).
- Fail-closed/fail-safe per tier: a filtering error must not crash the worker and must not silently disable an entire tier; follow the existing `DowntimeNextResult` / null-fallback error channels.
- Do not introduce a new `wl next` CLI flag if client-side filtering in the downtime deps suffices and keeps the change minimal; if a server-side filter is added, it must remain backward compatible.
- Preserve existing dispatched-marker, code-freeze, audit-freshness, and active-audit single-flight guards.

## Existing state

- Dispatcher tiers in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` + `packages/herdr/src/index.ts: createDowntimeDeps()`:
  - `getNextAuditCandidate` → `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only` → `selectAuditCandidate`
  - `getNextImplementCandidate` → `wl next --stage plan_complete --risk medium --effort medium -n 10` → `selectImplementCandidate`
  - `getNextItem('intake_complete'/'idea')` → `wl next --stage <stage> -n 10` → `selectNextCandidate` (with plan/intake dispatched-marker change-guard)
  - `getNextCriticalCandidate` → `wl list --priority critical --status open -n 10` → `selectCriticalCandidate` + `resolveDependencyFrontier`
  - Leader coordination path: `dispatchFromCoordination` iterates the durable offer list, `fetchItem` (`wl show` enriched) per entry, tier classification, shared `recordDispatch`/`spawnAgentPane` path.
- None of these filters currently check `needsProducerReview`; `wl list`/`wl next` server-side can filter by `needsProducerReview` (persistent-store `AND workitems.needsProducerReview = ?`) but the downtime deps do not pass it. Client-side `WorkItem.needsProducerReview` is available on every fetched item (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts: normalizeItem`).
- `needsProducerReview` is a tri-state integer → boolean (0/1, default 0) stored in `workitems` and surfaced via `wl list --needs-producer-review`.

## Desired change

- Filter `needsProducerReview === true` items out of every downtime selection path, client-side in the downtime deps (and, if justified, server-side via `--needs-producer-review false` on the `wl` queries):
  - `getNextAuditCandidate`, `getNextImplementCandidate`, `getNextItem`, `getNextCriticalCandidate` exclude review-gated candidates before `select*` (and re-check frontier blockers for critical).
  - Coordination leader path: `fetchItem` result with `needsProducerReview true` is skipped (not a dispatchable tier match) and the loop continues to the next offer entry.
- Treat `needsProducerReview` absent/null as dispatchable (explicit `=== true` check only).
- Add/extend tests in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` (and `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` for the leader path) covering: per-tier exclusion, frontier exclusion, leader skip, and flag-clear → dispatchable.
- Update downtime-worker header comment and inline tier comments to document the review-gate exclusion.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `createDowntimeDeps`: `getNextItem`, `getNextAuditCandidate`, `getNextImplementCandidate`, `getNextCriticalCandidate`, `fetchItem` wiring; where `needsProducerReview` filtering is added.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — tier orchestration (`dispatchDowntimeWork`, `dispatchFromCoordination`), header contract, per-tier selection helpers; docs + leader-loop handling.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.ts` — leader dispatch loop iterating the offer list (if separate from downtime-worker; otherwise within `downtime-worker.ts`).
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` / `src/persistent-store.ts` — server-side `needsProducerReview` filter (`AND workitems.needsProducerReview = ?`) if a CLI flag is passed through.
- `src/commands/next.ts` / `src/commands/list.ts` — `wl` CLI surface for `--needs-producer-review` if server-side filtering is used.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `WorkItem.needsProducerReview` normalization (already present; verify shape used by filters).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — regression tests for the new gate.

## Related work

- WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG — audit tier (completed/in_review without valid audit) — dispatch tier filtered here.
- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 — implement tier end-to-end (plan_complete risk/effort caps) — dispatch tier filtered here.
- WL-0MT3FM8VA005XBHE — critical items always progress first regardless of stage — critical-first tier + frontier resolver filtered here.
- WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY — dispatched-marker exclusion in audit-tier selection — existing selection-exclusion pattern this change follows.
- WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT — downtime dispatched-marker change-guard (RCA) — existing plan/intake exclusion pattern.
- WL-0MLGTWT4S1X4HDD9 / WL-0MLGTKW490NJTOAB — `--needs-producer-review` filter and Needs Producer Review flag — storage/query capability reused.
- WL-0MSN6Z9HN00637XY — flipping needsProducerReview must not make a valid audit stale — adjacent invariant to preserve.
- WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7 / WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL — coordination (leader offer list) path — leader per-entry classification filtered here.

Automated find_related report: see `find_related` step output persisted to `.worklog/tmp/` (if generated).

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: `needsProducerReview === true` means "human must act first — do not auto-dispatch for any skill (audit/implement/plan/intake)". If some tier should still dispatch (e.g. audit while awaiting review), that would need a separate follow-up item — ask rather than expanding scope.
- Assumption: filtering is `=== true` only; absent/false/undefined items are dispatchable. No tri-state "unknown = blocked" interpretation.
- Assumption: when every candidate in a tier needs review, the tier reports "no candidate" (not a `wl-error` strike) and dispatch falls through exactly as an empty backlog does — no cooldown triggered.
- Risk: adding filtering at both server and client layers could double-filter or mask errors; prefer client-side filtering first and add server-side flag only if it eliminates a meaningful batch-starvation window (batch is already `-n 10`).
- Risk: leader offer list could starve if every offered entry needs review — the leader must fall through gracefully and not pause with a no-candidate cooldown while review-gated items exist.
- Scope-creep risk: extending the flag's semantics (e.g., auto-clearing on review, new `wl next --needs-producer-review` default) is out of scope — record as separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should downtime dispatch skip items needing producer review? — Answer (operator): Yes — "When the downtime dispatcher selecting next issues to work on do not select work items marked as needing producer review." Source: intake seed text (`/intake` argument).
- Q: Which tiers does this apply to? — Answer (assumption documented, no question asked): All dispatch tiers (audit, implement, critical-first, plan, intake) and the coordination leader path. Reasonable default: review-gated items should not be auto-worked at any tier. Source: inferred from seed ("selecting next issues to work on" = all selection).
- Q: How does a flagged item become dispatchable again? — Answer (assumption documented, no question asked): Clearing the flag (`wl update <id> --needs-producer-review false`) makes it eligible again; the next idle poll may then select it. Source: existing flag semantics, no change to lifecycle.

# Intake Brief: Fair round-robin work scheduling with priority override (WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V)

## Problem Statement
The `dispatchFromCoordination` leader path in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` selects from the shared coordination file (`downtime-coordination.json`) by iterating entries in file order within each tier. With multiple projects contributing (ContextHub, SorraAgents, AI_Hell, Tableau-Card-Engine), this allows the same project to monopolise consecutive dispatch slots. We need globally-fair distribution with an exception for critical-priority items.

## Users

- **Agent — Automated downtime worker (primary):** As a downtime worker I want dispatches to fairly represent all contributing projects, so that no single project starves others of agent attention.
- **Developer / Project owner:** As a developer with work in an unserved project, I want the scheduler to eventually assign my project's candidate even when another project has more frequent offers, so that my backlog makes progress.

### User Stories
- As the downtime dispatcher leader, when entries exist from multiple projects at the same tier, I select the project whose last dispatch (in any tier) is oldest (round-robin), so that projects get a fair share of slots.
- As a project owner with a `critical`-priority offer on file, my next dispatch should bypass round-robin and run immediately (still at its stage-appropriate skill), so that urgent work is not delayed by fairness.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `dispatchFromCoordination` selects across the shared coordination entries in **global cross-project round-robin** order: among equally-eligible (tier-matched, non-critical) entries, the project whose `worklogRoot` was least-recently dispatched (with persistence across leader restarts / cycles) is chosen first. New / unknown roots sort first (never penalised). A single persistent cursor/state per worklog root (e.g. in a JSON file alongside the coordination file) drives the ordering; concurrent leaders do not corrupt the cursor (fail-open).
- [ ] When **any** entry on file is a `critical`-priority open item at a dispatchable stage (`idea` / `intake_complete` / `plan_complete` within caps; stage-appropriate skill), the leader dispatches that critical entry **immediately** ahead of all non-critical entries, regardless of round-robin position. Within the critical subset, selection remains deterministic (existing priority/sortIndex tie-break — one item per project, so round-robin is not needed inside critical).
- [ ] The critical override is **global** (evaluated before any tier loop): a critical in `plan_complete` outranks a non-critical `audit`, and a critical `idea` outranks a non-critical `implement`, matching the intent "jump to the front of the queue". The existing freeze (audit/implement skipped while frozen) and caps (`risk <= Medium && effort <= Medium` for `plan_complete`, including critical) are retained.
- [ ] After a successful dispatch (or a `spawn-failed`/`marker-write-failed` claim that still consumes the entry), the round-robin cursor/state advances to mark that project's `worklogRoot` as most-recently served, so the next dispatch in **any** tier starts from the following project.
- [ ] Existing `downtime-worker` and `coordination` tests still pass, plus new tests prove: (a) with two non-critical entries from different projects at the same tier, consecutive dispatches alternate projects; (b) a newly-arrived critical from project B is dispatched next even though round-robin would choose project A; (c) cursor persists across a simulated leader restart.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints
- Must build on the existing coordination machinery (`packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` lock + atomic write, `machine-coordination.ts` single machine dir) — no new daemon or external dependency.
- Fail-open on missing/corrupt round-robin state (behaves as if no history — original file order), never throws or starves dispatch.
- No behaviour change to `wl next` / single-project flows; this is strictly the multi-project leader path (`coordinationDir` present).
- Preserve dispatched-marker exclusion and CAS claim ordering already in `dispatchFromCoordination`.
- Each project currently registers at most one offer per cycle, so per-project multiplicity can be treated as one entry per root — design should not break if that grows, but need not optimise for many-per-root.

## Existing State
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchFromCoordination` groups fetched entries by tier (`audit` → `critical` → `implement` → `plan` → `intake`) and iterates each group in file order (`entries` array order). No cross-project fairness: repeated offers from the same root can win every slot when they re-queue quickly.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin.ts` provides a per-tier persistent cursor for the *legacy* `selectWithRotation` path (unused in coordination mode); the new requirement is **global, cross-tier** round-robin across `worklogRoot`s.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` manages `downtime-coordination.json` with atomic tmp+rename and an `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` lock (`tryAcquireCoordLock` / `withCoordLock`), and already carries `worklogRoot` per entry; `machine-coordination.ts` makes the file machine-wide.
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination-cross-root.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin.test.ts`.
- Contributing projects: ContextHub, SorraAgents, AI_Hell, Tableau-Card-Engine (each instance writes one entry via `runCoordinationCheckIn`).

## Desired Change
- Introduce a **global per-project round-robin** ordering for `dispatchFromCoordination`: track last-dispatched `worklogRoot` (persistent JSON alongside the coordination file, e.g. `downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`), sort same-tier eligible candidates by "least-recently-served first" before dispatch, and advance the cursor on each consumed entry.
- Promote the **critical override** to a global pre-tier check: re-fetch → if any dispatchable critical exists, dispatch the first critical immediately (respecting freeze/caps), before the tier-ordered round-robin loop.
- Add/extend tests to cover alternating-project fairness, critical jump-ahead, and cursor durability; update `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and relevant code comments.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Needs updated `dispatchFromCoordination` + new helpers for global round-robin ordering / cursor advance
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — May gain small helpers or remain unchanged (new state file is separate)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin.ts` — May be reused/extended or a new `downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` added for worklogRoot-keyed persistence
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — Reference for machine-dir resolution used by the new state file
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — Needs new fair-scheduling test cases
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — Needs updated dispatch ordering description (fair scheduling + critical override)

## Related Work
- Parent area: `WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL` (Refactor Downtime Dispatcher: leader election + shared coordination file), `WL-0MTF0KLO10043YAN` (Single machine-wide leader), `WL-0MTII45EP002DWK6` (Cross-directory tier dispatch)
- Preceding round-robin work: `WL-0MSSRED76008LGB6` + `downtime-round-robin.ts` / `downtime-round-robin.test.ts` (per-tier cursor, now superseded by global root-level rotation)
- Tier / dispatch reference: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:COORDINATION_TIER_ORDER`, `classifyItemForDispatch`, `COORDINATION_FILE` / `readCoordinationFile` in `coordination.ts`
- Follow-up opportunity: if per-root multiplicity grows beyond one, consider weighted or deficit round-robin (record as a linked work item, not in scope)

## Risks & Assumptions
- **Risk:** Cursor file races between leaders → Mitigation: reuse the existing `withCoordLock` / tmp+rename pattern; fail-open when lock is contended.
- **Risk:** New critical items arriving between fetch and dispatch could be missed → Mitigation: critical check happens on the same single fetch pass; subsequent arrivals wait one cycle (acceptable at 30-min check-in cadence).
- **Risk:** Stale-entry pruning removes a root before its round-robin turn → Mitigation: pruned roots drop from ordering automatically; no ghost cursor entries block others.
- **Risk:** Scope creep (e.g. per-entry priority weighting beyond critical) → Mitigation: explicitly out of scope; non-critical priorities are treated as equally round-robined (per operator: one item per project).
- **Assumption:** At most one entry per `worklogRoot` per cycle — holds today; ordering by `worklogRoot` last-served is equivalent to ordering by entry last-served.
- **Assumption:** "Jump to the front" means dispatch before any non-critical regardless of tier, not just within the same tier — confirmed with operator (clarification round: globally, dispatch immediately).
- **Assumption:** Persistence should survive leader restarts and machine reboot → file on disk in the machine coordination dir, not in-memory only.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "What constitutes a 'project' for fair scheduling?" — Answer (user): "The multi-project downtime scheduling recently implemented — leader election with one work item per project via the herdr extension. Currently ContextHub, ../SorraAgents, ../AI_Hell, ../Tableau-Card-Engine." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Is this about `wl next` or the coordination dispatch?" — Answer (user): "The multi-project case — nothing to do with `wl next`." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "When a project has a critical item, does it jump the queue?" — Answer (user): "yes" (affirmative — critical from any project jumps ahead). Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Do non-critical priorities (high/medium/low) matter within round-robin?" — Answer (user): "I believe each project only registers a single work item so this is not important." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Round-robin scope — per-tier or globally?" — Answer (user): "globally" Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.

**Goal:** Wire the global cursor into coordination dispatch for non-critical entries and advance it on consume.

- Added imports: `loadRoundRobinCursor` and `advanceRoot` from `downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts`

- Non-critical tier dispatched/spawn-failed/marker-write-failed: calls `removeEntry` + `advanceRoundRobinCursor`

- Cursor module (downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts) not modified — consumed as dependency

# Downtime dispatcher: make wl-error pauses debuggable

## Problem

Between 01:00–06:12 UTC on 2026-09-02 the TCE per-worklog `downtime-dispatches.log` showed 5 aggregate pauses:

> `Downtime worker: 3 consecutive wl CLI errors — pausing dispatch for 3600000ms.`

with successful dispatches interleaved (01:47 audit, 02:14 implement, 02:44 intake, 03:14 audit, 03:47 implement, 04:14 plan, 05:44 implement) — proving transient failures. **No per-strike detail is retained**, so "what was the wl error?" cannot be answered from logs.

Root cause: the 3-strike pause only logs once (at strike 3). The `DowntimeErrorEvent` type (`downtime-worker.ts:1238`) has `error?: string` but it carries only a plain string — not structured stderr/exitCode/timeout/workItemId/probe context. `pauseAfterPersistentErrors()` (`downtime-worker.ts:2793`) is called with the fixed message `wl CLI errors — pausing dispatch…` (`downtime-worker.ts:3210`), discarding the `Error` built from `stderr||stdout||error.message` at `fetcher.ts:372` and the per-entry `result.ok===false` skip at `downtime-worker.ts:1634` / `wl-error` outcome at 1559. Only the 3-strike aggregate is written via `deps.recordError()` → `appendDowntimeLogEntry()` (`index.ts:998` / `downtime-log.ts:268`), with no stderr/exitCode/timeoutMs/workItemId/probe context.

Machine-wide dispatch is now authoritative (`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` + `downtime-leader-lease.json`), but logs stay per-worklog (`downtime-log.ts:5` F6 WL-0MTII4CWT00452HU + `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md:222`) for per-project observability — aggregate + per-strike logs must both be queryable.

## Users

- **Operator on-call**: Needs to grep `downtime-dispatches.log` and immediately see what went wrong (stderr snippet, exit code, timeout) on each failed strike, not just the pause summary.
- **Debugging engineer**: Needs to distinguish coordination probe failures (empty-file transient gap) from CLI failures (TIMEOUT, SQLITE_BUSY, parse error) to triage root cause.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Per-strike logging**: A 3-strike pause produces 1 pause line + 3 per-strike log lines, each with parseable `stderr` excerpt (truncated to 200 chars), `exitCode`, `timeoutMs`, and `workItemId`, visible via `grep wl-error */.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`.
2. **Probe-context distinction**: Log entries distinguish "worklog probe failed while shared coordination file held no dispatchable entry" from "wl CLI errors" so operators can tell `empty-file transient gap` vs `CLI failure`.
3. **Schema bounded, fail-closed**: `DowntimeErrorEvent` schema enriched with structured fields; rolling-log trimming still bounded (`DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES=100`); write failure never crashes the worker (fail-closed).
4. **Tests**: Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` / `downtime-log.test.ts` assert per-strike logging and field presence; `npm run build` and full project suite green.
5. **Docs updated**: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` includes log-schema table and troubleshooting note for aggregating global dispatches across per-worklog logs.

## Constraints

- Must not change the pause cooldown duration (`DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_NO_CANDIDATE_COOLDOWN_MS=3600000`) or strike limit (`DOWNTIME_ERROR_STRIKE_LIMIT=3`).
- Must not change the coordination-leadership model (machine-wide dispatch stays authoritative).
- Rolling log bounded to `DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES=100`; large stderr snippets truncated.
- Write failures fail-closed (never crash the worker).

## Existing State

- `DowntimeErrorEvent` (`downtime-worker.ts:1238`) has `cwd`, `at`, `message`, `error?: string`.
- `pauseAfterPersistentErrors(message, error?)` (`downtime-worker.ts:2793`) only calls `recordError` when `errorStrikes >= 3`.
- Called at `downtime-worker.ts:3186` (probe failure, no error arg) and `downtime-worker.ts:3210` (wl error, `outcome.error` only).
- `DOWNTIME_ERROR_STRIKE_LIMIT=3`, `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_NO_CANDIDATE_COOLDOWN_MS=3600000`.

## Desired Change

- Enrich `DowntimeErrorEvent` with structured fields: `stderrExcerpt` (≤200 chars), `exitCode`, `timeoutMs`, `workItemId`, `command`, `attempt` (1/2/3), `probeContext` (coordination probe vs dispatch path).
- Log **every** wl-error strike (1, 2, and 3) to the rolling JSONL, not just the 3rd, while retaining the existing pause marker for alerting.
- Update `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md` downtime section to document new fields and how to aggregate `*/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` vs `~/.herdr/downtime/` state.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `pauseAfterPersistentErrors` (2793), `dispatchFromCoordination` (1559), `computeMostImportantItem` probe (2896)
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `runWl` error formatting (372), timeouts (`CLAIM_TIMEOUT_MS`, `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS=60000`)
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `DowntimeErrorEvent` type import, `recordError` (1036), `DOWNTIME_WL_TIMEOUT_MS`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — rolling JSONL, `DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES`, `COORDINATION_LOG_FILE` vs dispatch log
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — per-strike logging tests
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts` — schema and bounded trimming tests
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — log-schema table, troubleshooting
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — downtime section

## Related Work

- WL-0MTII4CWT00452HU — F6 migration: machine-wide dispatch authoritative (completed)
- WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8 — Log herdr downtime dispatches (completed)
- WL-0MTOSJZT0002VZNK — Add central machine-wide dispatch log (open, related)
- WL-0MTJE0X8O0061KSD — Docs: update downtime dispatcher docs (completed)
- WL-0MSZS1NNV0075NFI — Header rendering: `[Downtime Off]` status text (completed)
- WL-0MSZ4NSOE007AQEF — Shortcut key to toggle downtime dispatch per herdr instance (completed)
- Find-related report: WL-0MSG7ZTC000163FL (Downtime worker test suite), WL-0MQOIBTHR002VMEK (Guardrails), WL-0MRSGMTYY0062WFJ (wl audit-set)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Stderr size**: stderr may be very large; truncate to 200 chars with `[truncated]` marker. Assumed safe.
- **Log format change**: Adding new structured fields changes the JSONL schema; older consumers may see extra fields (tolerant). Assumed backward compatible.
- **Error string already exists**: `DowntimeErrorEvent.error?: string` is already present but plain — the change enriches it with structured fields rather than replacing.
- **Per-strike volume**: 3 strikes × 5 pauses = 15 new lines; rolling limit (100 entries) handles volume. No concern.
- **Scope creep**: This is logging/observability only; does not change dispatch logic, cooldowns, or leadership model.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

- Q: Should `stderrExcerpt` truncate at a specific character count? — Answer: 200 chars with `[truncated]` marker. Source: risk assessment, reasonable default for log lines.
- Q: What is the `command` field in per-strike logs? — Answer: The wl subcommand that failed (e.g., `wl show <id>`, `wl close <id>`). Source: context from `fetcher.ts` `runWl` calls.
- Q: Should the pause line itself be enhanced with per-strike summary? — Answer: Yes, but the primary requirement is 3 per-strike lines. Source: AC1, pause line is for alerting.

# Dispatch-logs Skill

## Problem
Operators investigating overnight dispatches must know the machine-wide vs per-worklog log architecture, then aggregate `*/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` across projects themselves. There is no single command to produce a 24h dispatch report.

## Desired skill
A `dispatch-logs` skill in the ContextHub project (`.pi/skills/dispatch-logs/`) that, when invoked via `/skill:dispatch-logs` (or `skill:dispatch-logs --hours 6 --since 2026-09-01T20:00:00Z --project ContextHub`), produces a concise human-readable report of all dispatch activity.

### Default behaviour
- Window: last 24 hours from `Date.now()`.
- Search all worklog roots for files matching `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`.
- Parse each file for lines matching `Downtime worker:` or `Dispatch completed` or `ERROR` or `DOWNTIME`.
- Also read `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` and `downtime-leader-lease.json` for leader identity and active dispatch target.
- Produce a report with:
  1. **Leader summary** — leader ID, acquired-at, active project, leader lock file.
  2. **Dispatch timeline** — chronological list of all dispatches with timestamp, project root, dispatch type (audit/implement/plan/intake), work-item ID, and status.
  3. **Error summary** — consecutive-wl-error pauses, timestamps, duration, and project.
  4. **Coordination state** — current coordination file contents (leader, active project, last dispatch).
  5. **Known issues** — if per-strike detail is missing, note that per-strike stderr/exitCode are not available yet (tracked by companion debug item).

### Invocation
```
/skill:dispatch-logs                  # default: last 24h, all projects
/skill:dispatch-logs --hours 6        # last 6 hours
/skill:dispatch-logs --since 2026-09-01T20:00:00Z --until 2026-09-02T02:00:00Z  # custom window
/skill:dispatch-logs --project ContextHub  # single project
/skill:dispatch-logs --json           # machine-readable output
```

### Implementation
- SKILL.md: frontmatter with name, description, and invocation instructions.
- `scripts/dispatch-logs.py`: Python script that:
  1. Parses arguments (`--hours`, `--since`, `--until`, `--project`, `--json`).
  2. Discovers project roots by finding all `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` files (walk from `~` or configured locations; skip `node_modules`, `dist`, `build`).
  3. Reads and parses log files (JSONL format, one object per line).
  4. Reads machine coordination state from `~/.herdr/downtime/`.
  5. Produces the formatted report.
- Test: `tests/dispatch-logs.test.py` — unit tests for parsing, argument handling, and report structure (mock log files).

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `/skill:dispatch-logs` produces a human-readable 24h report covering all projects on this machine.
- [ ] --hours, --since/--until, --project, and --json flags work correctly.
- [ ] Report includes leader summary, dispatch timeline, error summary, and coordination state.
- [ ] Graceful handling when no dispatch logs exist (empty report, not error).
- [ ] Unit tests pass for parsing and formatting.
- [ ] SKILL.md documents the skill and invocation patterns.

### Related
- Debug item: WL-0MTJPYM53003ORCV — "make wl-error pauses debuggable" (companion; skill notes missing per-strike detail).
- Machine-wide dispatch architecture: `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json`, leader lease, per-worklog logs.

# Investigate downtime dispatcher vs herdr selection list divergence (WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q)

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher consistently selects and dispatches work items that do not appear in the herdr extensions selection list, so two first-class "next most important item" selectors disagree. The project needs a diagnosed root cause for the divergence and a producer-reviewed determination of which ranking (if either) correctly identifies the most important item, before any fix is scoped.

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — needs a single trustworthy "most important" ordering to decide what to work on and whether downtime dispatch is helping or harming prioritization.
- **Agent / herdr user** browsing `prefix+l` — relies on the herdr list as the visible priority queue; unexpected downtime work on off-list items erodes trust in the list.
- **Maintainer of wl next / herdr / downtime-worker** — needs a clear contract for how the two selectors should relate (shared vs intentionally different).

Example user stories:
- "As a producer, I want the downtime dispatcher and the herdr list to agree on priority, so automated work tracks my intent."
- "As a herdr user, when downtime dispatches `/skill:implement WL-XYZ`, I want WL-XYZ to have been visible in the herdr list, so I understand why it was chosen."
- "As a maintainer, I want a documented ranking contract so I can tell whether a divergence is a bug or an intentional tier policy."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Divergence diagnosed with evidence** — the brief/records cite the exact code paths compared (herdr `fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` + `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` + `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` vs downtime `downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork` + `src/commands/next.ts` + `packages/shared/src/database.ts:filterCandidates/findNextWorkItemFromItems/computeScore/reSort`) and a reproducible sample where the two selectors disagree (e.g. `wl next -n N` output vs herdr rendered list vs downtime tier chosen).
2. **Ranking gap mapped** — each material difference is listed: input sets/caps (`wl next -n` cap 32 + mandatory merge vs stage-scoped `wl next --stage …` per tier + `wl list` for audit), stage/risk/effort filters, audit-tier recency/marker/code-freeze gates, blocked/in_review handling, `sortIndex`/reSort/recency-policy, and grouping vs flat ordering.
3. **"Most important" determination recorded and producer-reviewed** — the work item records which selector (herdr list, dispatcher tier order, or `wl next` score) is judged authoritative for "most important" and why, with an explicit producer sign-off comment; if neither is authoritative, the desired unified ranking is described.
4. **Follow-up work item(s) filed only after review** — no fix is implemented in this investigation; at most, one or more follow-up work items are created *after* producer review to align or intentionally diverge the selectors, with the resolution direction noted on this item.
5. **Documentation/tests note** — the investigation updates or points to the doc that will carry the ranking contract (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` / herdr README / `src/commands/next.ts` help), and any sampling scripts are reproducible.

## Constraints

- Investigation only — do not change ranking code in this item; any code change requires a separate work item after producer review.
- Do not assume which selector is correct; ask the producer when the evidence is ambiguous.
- Respect ignore rules; keep questions high-signal (≤3 per round).
- All description/comments in Markdown; escape only backticks.

## Existing state

- **Herdr list:** `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` runs `wl next -n N --include-in-progress` (auto `reSort` unless `--no-re-sort`), merges mandatory subsets from `wl list --priority critical --root-only` and `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only` via `fetchMandatorySubsets`, applies `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` (root-only, `stage != done`, mandatory always shown, `browseItemCount` limits only "other" items), and regroups with `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` / `assignItemGroups` (critical Group N / Group N / Idea / Other / In Review, file-path conflict partitioning). Rendering via `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.

- **wl next ranking (shared):** `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `reSort()` = `getAllOrderedByScore(recencyPolicy)` → `assignSortIndexValues`; `computeScore` weights priority×1000, `blocksHighPriority` +500, `in_review` +600, age/effort/recency, blocked −10000, in-progress multipliers; audit-not-ready fresh boost +3500 (non-critical only); `filterCandidates` pipeline (stage → deleted → completed/done/in_review preservation → in_progress → excluded → assignee/search → risk/effort at-most → dep-blocked); `handleCriticalEscalation` (unblocked criticals first, then blocked-critical blockers), non-critical blocker surfacing, open-item `selectBySortIndex` (sortIndex or effective-priority tie-break). `src/commands/next.ts` auto reSort with `--recency-policy` (default `ignore`) and risk/effort filters.

- **Downtime dispatcher:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork` — tier order: audit (`wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only` within 7-day recency, no valid audit within 7d, root-only, durable dispatched-marker exclusion, active-audit single-flight), implement (`wl next --stage plan_complete --risk ≤Medium --effort ≤Medium`, open + blocked filtering), plan (`wl next --stage intake_complete`), fallback idea (`wl next --stage idea`); pre-dispatch CAS claim (`--if-status/--if-stage`), per-process single-flight, code-freeze tri-state gate (frozen/ambiguous skips audit+implement, reports `code-freeze`/`fresh-audit-skip`/`audit-in-flight`/`wl-error`/`no-candidate`), scheduled-prompts tier, round-robin tie-break, 60-min no-candidate cooldown, 3-strike `wl-error` pause, per-worklog rolling log + machine-wide coordination lease.

- Observed sample (2026-09-02): `wl next -n 20` returned Idea-group high-priority items (e.g. WL-0MT... high/idea) while herdr's mandatory set adds 19 `in_review` + critical groups; dispatcher tiers can select items outside the herdr window due to stage/risk scoping and audit-tier `wl list` source.

## Desired change

For this investigation: a producer-reviewed brief on this work item that (a) explains why the two selectors diverge, (b) judges which (if either) currently picks the most important item, and (c) scopes the follow-up direction (unify on `wl next` score vs keep intentional tier divergence vs new contract). No code change in this item.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — herdr list fetch: `wl next -n` + mandatory `wl list` merge + `selectWorkItems`/`regroupWorkItems`
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — mandatory-always logic (critical ∪ completed/in_review, root-only, done excluded)
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — `assignItemGroups`/`regroupWorkItems` ordering (Critical Group N / Group N / Idea / Other / In Review)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — list rendering consuming grouped selection
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier orchestration, claim/marker/freeze gates
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `computeScore`/`filterCandidates`/`findNextWorkItemFromItems`/`handleCriticalEscalation`/`reSort`/`selectBySortIndex`
- `src/commands/next.ts` / `src/commands/grouping.ts` — `wl next` entry point, auto reSort, stage/risk/effort filters, group assignment
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` / `packages/herdr/README.md` / `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — ranking/coordination contract docs

## Related work

- **WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX** — counts in Herdr selection list are incorrect (open, high) — reporting that the list's top-N vs group totals disagree ( symptom of mandatory-merge/wl-next-cap interaction)
- **WL-0MS8XL3EW006Y04G** — Herdr selection list: smart selection (completed) — introduced mandatory-always + fetch merge

- **WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 / WL-0MSMAIP5F003WAGG** — implement tier + risk/effort filters as wired into `wl next` and downtime dispatch

# Dispatcher consumes Herdr selection list head (WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2)

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork`) and the Herdr extension selection list (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` → `worklist.ts`) disagree on "most important item" because the dispatcher maintains its own tier ordering (`wl next --stage …` per tier + `wl list` audit query) instead of reusing the Herdr list. The project needs the dispatcher to consume the Herdr list head so the two selectors agree by construction. Supersedes prior "unify on `wl next`" scope per producer determination WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1 (2026-09-02).

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — needs a single trustworthy queue; the item dispatched during downtime was visible at the top of `prefix+l` and reflects declared prioritization intent.
- **Herdr user browsing `prefix+l`** — expects downtime work to track exactly what the visible list shows, so automated work does not appear arbitrary.
- **Maintainer of herdr / downtime-worker / wl next** — needs a single ranking contract; ranking logic lives only in the fetcher/smart-selection/grouping/database pipeline.

Example user stories:
- As a producer, I want the downtime dispatcher to pick the first item shown in the Herdr list, so automated work follows the priority I already see.
- As a herdr user, when downtime dispatches `/skill:implement WL-XYZ`, I want WL-XYZ to have been at the head of the Herdr list, so I understand why it was chosen.
- As a maintainer, I want the ranking contract documented as "dispatcher == Herdr list head" so future safety gates are evaluated as filters, not a competing ranking.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Dispatcher consumes Herdr list head** — `dispatchDowntimeWork` (and any coordination-leader path) derives its candidate from the Herdr selection list head rather than a separate tier ordering / stage-scoped `wl next` / `wl list` audit query. No second ranking implementation remains on the dispatch path.
2. **No duplicate ranking; gates are filters** — tier ordering / `wl next --stage` per-tier calls / audit `wl list` ranking are no longer used to pick "most important". Any safety gates that must remain (code-freeze skip, dispatched-marker exclusion, active-audit single-flight, per-process single-flight / CAS claim) act as sequential filters on the Herdr-ordered candidates. If no Herdr-ordered candidate passes the filters, the dispatcher reports "no candidate" rather than falling back to a separate ranking.
3. **Herdr list remains sole ranking path** — `fetchNextItems` / `selectWorkItems` / `regroupWorkItems` stay the sole ranking path (mandatory-always for critical + `completed`/`in_review`, `browseItemCount` windowing of "other" items, grouping logic, `reSort`/`computeScore` as used by the fetcher). No `wl next`/`database.ts` scoring change is required to fix the divergence; if `fetchNextItems` delegates to `wl next` internally that internal detail is acceptable — the observable contract is "dispatcher == Herdr list head".
4. **Contract documented** — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md` (and `src/commands/next.ts` help if it references dispatcher selection) state explicitly: dispatcher selects the first dispatchable item from the Herdr selection list; any remaining safety override (e.g. code-freeze) is documented as a skip/filter on that sequence, not a ranking.
5. **No regression; observable agreement proven** — existing `wl next` / herdr fetcher/grouping / downtime-worker fixtures pass; a reproducible sampling script shows `wl next -n` / Herdr list / downtime pick agree (downtime picks the list head after filtering) on a fixture. Dispatched-marker / code-freeze / single-flight gating still respected as filters on the Herdr sequence.

## Constraints

- Zero npm deps for herdr; `smart-selection.ts`/`grouping.ts` duplicated per TUI stays in sync with `src/commands/*` if touched.
- `browseItemCount` clamping (1–50) and root-only / `done`-exclusion rules respected.
- Do not fork a second ranking; reuse the Herdr list pipeline.
- Investigation only touched the prior item (WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q); this item carries the implementation.
- Backwards compat: existing dispatched-marker / code-freeze gating semantics preserved as filters.

## Existing state

- **Herdr list:** `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` runs `wl next -n N --include-in-progress` (auto `reSort` unless `--no-re-sort`), merges mandatory subsets via `fetchMandatorySubsets` (`wl list --priority critical --root-only` and `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only`), applies `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` (root-only, `stage != done`, mandatory always shown, `browseItemCount` limits only "other" items), and regroups with `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` / `assignItemGroups` (Critical Group N / Group N / Idea / Other / In Review). Rendered via `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- **Downtime dispatcher:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork` — tier order audit → implement (`wl next --stage plan_complete` with risk/effort caps) → plan (`wl next --stage intake_complete`) → fallback idea (`wl next --stage idea`); audit tier uses `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only` with 7-day recency / dispatched-marker / active-audit / code-freeze gates; pre-dispatch CAS claim, per-process single-flight, scheduled-prompts tier, round-robin cursor, cooldowns.
- **Shared scoring:** `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (`computeScore`/`reSort`/`filterCandidates`/`findNextWorkItemFromItems`) and `src/commands/next.ts` auto `reSort` — shared by `wl next` but not required to change for this contract; the observable contract is Herdr list head.
- All divergence gaps mapped in WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q (cap 32 / mandatory merge / stage-scoped calls / audit `wl list` source / tier order / risk-effort gates / code-freeze tri-state, etc.) — eliminated by consuming the Herdr order directly.

## Desired change

Replace the dispatcher's independent tier ordering with consumption of the Herdr selection list head:

- Refactor `downtime-worker.ts` to invoke (or share code with) the Herdr fetcher/selection pipeline to obtain the ordered candidate sequence, then apply only the necessary safety filters (code-freeze, dispatched-marker, single-flight/active-audit) sequentially on that sequence.
- Remove or dead-code the tier-ordering / per-stage `wl next` / audit `wl list` ranking path from the dispatch decision (or leave only as unused fallback behind a feature flag with a clear deprecation note).
- Document the contract ("dispatcher == Herdr list head; filters, not ranking") in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — Herdr selection pipeline reused by dispatcher
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — mandatory-always + browseItemCount logic
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — regroupWorkItems / assignItemGroups ordering
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — rendering consuming grouped selection
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — dispatchDowntimeWork to be refactored to consume list head (+ fixtures)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — computeScore/reSort/filterCandidates as used by fetcher (not dispatcher ranking)
- `src/commands/next.ts` / `src/commands/grouping.ts` — wl next entry point as used by fetcher
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — dispatcher contract doc
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Herdr list contract doc

## Related work

- Investigation: WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q — downtime dispatcher vs herdr selection list divergence (producer determination revised 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1, superseding WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS) → follow-up direction is this item.
- WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX — counts in Herdr selection list are incorrect (symptom of cap/mandatory interaction; not blocking but shares fetcher context)
- WL-0MS8XL3EW006Y04G / WL-0MSKCRX730052iiw / WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G / WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR — Herdr smart selection / in_review / root-only rules shaping mandatory set
- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 / WL-0MSMAIP5F003WAGG — implement tier + risk/effort filters wired into wl next / dispatcher (removed or converted to filters in this work)
- WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY / WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN / WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8 — dispatched-marker exclusion, conditional claim, dispatch logging (preserved as filters)
- WL-0MSSRED76008LGB6 — priority-first with round-robin tie-break (cursor handling to reconcile with Herdr order)
- RCA docs: `downtime-redispatch-rca-2026-08-13.md`, `downtime-disable-incident-rca-2026-08-22.md` — prior tier/re-dispatch incidents

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: "selection list" means herdr `prefix+l` Work Items list (`fetchNextItems` path); "downtime dispatcher" means `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier loop in `downtime-worker.ts` (including coordination leader path if any).
- Assumption: producer wants a single notion of "most important" — confirmed 2026-09-02 (Herdr list canonical; dispatcher consumes head).
- Risk: code-freeze / audit safety behavior at head — if the list head must be skipped, the skip order must be explicit and remain a filter on the Herdr sequence; document clearly.
- Risk: `in_review` mandatory-always items in the list — dispatcher taking the head must still respect `completed`/`in_review` dispatchability; filter vs ranking distinction must be explicit to avoid re-dispatching audits.
- Risk: spare-capacity / idle-budget / round-robin cursor logic must be reconciled as filters or removed; otherwise a second ordering re-emerges.
- Scope-creep risk: unifying ranking touches herdr selection and downtime-worker — keep scope to dispatcher-consumes-head; do not rework scoring or grouping unless required for the contract. Extra opportunities → new work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When you say 'most important,' do you mean the Herdr list order or the dispatcher tier order?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1, rescoping WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2; supersedes WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS): **Herdr extension selection list order is authoritative** (`fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems`). Dispatcher selects the first item in that list — no second ranking. Source: producer comment WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1 on WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q.
- Q2: "Should the two selectors be unified to one shared ranking, or should the dispatcher intentionally differ (e.g. audit-first)?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1): **Unified on the Herdr list** — single source of truth; dispatcher consumes the list head. Supersedes prior "unify on `wl next`". Source: same producer determination.
- Q3: "For sampling, which `browseItemCount` / `wl next -n` window and which worklog root should be the reference?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS as affirmed by WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1): **LGTM** — default `browseItemCount` / ContextHub root / `wl next -n 20` accepted as sampling reference. Source: producer comment on WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q.

No open questions. Interview skipped — seed context and revised producer determination (WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1) already provide a clear, testable brief.

# Scheduled prompts: add time-of-day dispatch (time window) to scheduled-prompts tier

## Problem statement

The scheduled-prompts tier (WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX; `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, `templates/scheduled-prompts.json`) only supports best-effort frequency in whole days (`intervalDays` via `isDueScheduledPrompt`: due iff `now - lastTriggeredAt >= intervalDays`). There is no way to pin a prompt to a time of day, so a daily standup cannot be made to run at a specific wall-clock time (e.g. 06:05) and instead fires whenever the next idle slot appears after the interval elapses — too early/late for a daily standup window.

## Users

- Operators who want a prompt (notably the daily standup, `/skill:standup`) to run at a specific time of day, not just once per N days whenever an idle slot appears.

### User stories

- As an operator, I want to add an optional `time` field (e.g. `06:05`) to a scheduled-prompt entry so the system dispatches it in the first available idle window **after** that time, so the standup runs at 06:05 each day.
- As an operator, when `time` is absent the existing behaviour is unchanged (due iff `now - last >= intervalDays`), so existing entries like `/skill:refactor` keep working without config changes.
- As an operator, I want `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` and provisioned `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` to set `/skill:standup` to 06:05, so a fresh worklog gets the correct daily standup time.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add optional `time?: string` to `ScheduledPrompt` (`packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts`). When absent, behaviour is identical to today (backward-compatible). Valid values are wall-clock `HH:MM` 24-hour times (e.g. `06:05`); entries with an invalid `time` are skipped with a logged warning (fail-closed, never a crash), consistent with invalid `intervalDays`/prompt handling (AC7 of WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX).
2. Extend due-check semantics (`isDueScheduledPrompt` / `getDueScheduledPrompt`): an entry with `time` is due only when BOTH (a) `now - lastTriggeredAt >= intervalDays * DAY_MS` (same interval gate as today) AND (b) `now` is at or after the `time` on the calendar day of `now` (local wall-clock). If `now` is before `time` today and the interval gate is otherwise satisfied, the entry is NOT due — it becomes due in the first idle window at/after `time`. A dispatched entry is NOT due again until the next calendar day's `time` has been reached and the interval has again elapsed (so a 06:05 daily entry dispatched at 07:00 today is not due again at 08:00 today).
3. `lastTriggeredAt` semantics ensure once-per-interval: after a timed dispatch, the interval comparison uses the actual dispatch time, so a missed `time` (e.g. no idle slot until 08:00) still counts as dispatched for that day and the next due time is tomorrow 06:05 (not 08:00 tomorrow and not immediately). Daily entries with `time` therefore fire at most once per calendar day.
4. Update `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` to include `/skill:standup` with `intervalDays: 1` and `time: "06:05"` (the canonical standup time). `src/commands/init.ts` provisioning remains create-if-absent; `wl init` on an existing repo must not clobber user edits — if the operator has customised scheduled prompts, re-running `wl init` leaves them untouched. New worklogs provisioned after this change get the timed standup entry.
5. Ensure `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` in the current checkout reflects `time: "06:05"` for `/skill:standup` (so the dev branch's live config matches the template).
6. Update documentation/comments to describe the `time` field (README / `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` header / `PLUGIN_GUIDE.md` or equivalent downtime docs) and the "first window after time" semantics, including the backward-compat note when `time` is absent and the local wall-clock interpretation of `HH:MM`.
7. Unit/integration tests cover: parse of `time` (valid, absent, invalid → skipped), due-check with `time` (before-time not due, at/after-time due, interval gate interaction, once-per-day, missed-window becomes tomorrow), backward-compat (no `time` behaves as before), and the timed standup entry in the provisioned template.
8. Full project test suite passes with the new changes (no regressions).

## Constraints

- Follow the worker's existing fail-closed philosophy at every boundary: never dispatch, never throw (mirrors WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX constraints and `scheduled-prompts.ts` header).
- `time` is wall-clock local `HH:MM` (no timezone field, no cron); `lastTriggeredAt` remains UTC ISO-8601 as today. The due check interprets `time` against local calendar day.
- Scheduled tier remains the first dispatch tier, gated by the same fresh-read code-freeze marker; per-process single-flight guard still applies. No new timer infrastructure — reuse `createDowntimeWorker.tick`.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — `ScheduledPrompt` (id/prompt/intervalDays/lastTriggeredAt), `parseScheduledPrompt`, `isDueScheduledPrompt`, `getDueScheduledPrompt`, `DAY_MS`; no `time` field.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork` scheduled tier (freeze gate → scheduled → audit → …); `dispatchScheduledPrompt` with atomic `lastTriggeredAt` persist + rolling-log `scheduled` kind.
- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` + `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` — base set is `/skill:refactor` (intervalDays 3) plus `/skill:standup` (intervalDays 1) with no `time`.
- `src/commands/init.ts` — provisions `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` from the template, create-if-absent (never clobber).

## Desired change

Extend `ScheduledPrompt` with optional `time: "HH:MM"` and update the due-check to be "interval gate AND at-or-after time today" so timed entries dispatch in the first idle window after their wall-clock time. Set the canonical standup time to `06:05` in both the template and the live `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`. Update docs/tests accordingly. When `time` is absent, behaviour is identical to today.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — add `time` field, validation, due-check extension.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — no structural change expected (consumes via `getDueScheduledPrompt`), but verify tier interaction / dispatch semantics for timed entries.
- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` — add `time: "06:05"` to `/skill:standup`.
- `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` — add `time: "06:05"` to `/skill:standup` in the checkout so the dev branch reflects the template.
- `src/commands/init.ts` — no change expected beyond carrying the new template value (create-if-absent preserved).
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.test.ts` or `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` / `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — new/updated tests for `time` parse + due-check.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` / `PLUGIN_GUIDE.md` / `CONFIG.md` / `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` header — document `time` field and "first window after time" semantics.

## Related work

- WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX — scheduled prompts tier (parent capability).
- Standup skill: `/skill:standup` + `generate_standup.py` (scheduled via this tier; canonical consumer of `06:05`).
- WL-0MTF5UAJ4000LLZ9 — provisioning / scheduled-prompts template.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: `time` is `HH:MM` local wall-clock on the calendar day of `now`; seconds are not needed. `lastTriggeredAt` remains UTC — the due check bridges them by comparing the local clock for `time` against `now` and the interval against `lastTriggeredAt`.
- Risk: "first window after time" depends on an idle slot appearing; if the machine is busy all day, the dispatch slips to the next idle window (still at most once per day due to `lastTriggeredAt` anchoring). This is the correct best-effort behaviour.
- Risk: DST / system clock skew — acceptable for best-effort `HH:MM` local semantics; clock-skew handling mirrors `isDueScheduledPrompt` today (future `lastTriggeredAt` → not due).
- Scope creep: cron expressions, timezone-aware schedules, per-entry model overrides — record separately, not this item.

## Problem statement

Downtime coordination entries expire via `pruneStaleEntries(coordinationDir, leaseTtlMs)` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchFromCoordination` (`leaseTtlMs = DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS*1000 = 300s`). But `runCoordinationCheckIn` re-offers only every `DEFAULT_COORDINATION_CHECK_IN_MS = 30min`. A non-leader's entry is offered at most once per 30min yet is pruned after 5min if no dispatch consumes it — 25min dead window where the leader sees no entry for that project.

Overnight this starved SorraAgents while ContextHub dispatched alone every ~30min (verified Sep 4: SorraAgents offered `SA-0MSQ6K7Z1002H14Z` at 06:39:39 -> dispatched 06:39:41 only when offer was fresh; earlier offers at 23:45,00:08,00:38 etc. were pruned before the next idle dispatch). The `critical first then round-robin (per-worklogRoot)` guarantee (`WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V` + =`WL-0MTJE0FXC006WAOX`) never got a chance — `sortEntriesByRoundRobin` only orders entries that are present.

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — expects global `critical first, then round-robin across projects` as documented; overnight bias to one project erodes trust and delays other projects' ready work.
- **Herdr user with multiple project tabs open** — wants spare-capacity dispatch shared fairly, not oversubscribing one project's backlog.
- **Maintainer of herdr / downtime-worker / wl** — needs a single consistent contract for cross-project dispatch without TTL/check-in mismatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Expiry removed** — `pruneStaleEntries` (and any equivalent TTL prune on `downtime-coordination.json`) is removed or disabled for the machine coordination file. No coordination entry is removed solely by wall-clock age. Legacy per-worklog files (if still read) follow the same rule.
2. **Dispatch checks current eligibility** — before dispatching, the dispatcher re-fetches the work item via `fetchItem(workItemId, worklogRoot)` and verifies it is still in a dispatchable state (`classifyItemForDispatch` / `isAuditFresh` / stage+status that needs work). A stale entry (item now closed/in_progress/done, audit now fresh, or otherwise not dispatchable) is treated as non-dispatchable: its entry is removed, the cursor is not advanced for it, and the dispatcher continues to the next entry — no pane spawned, no marker written.
   - Existing safety gates preserved as filters: code-freeze skip, dispatched-marker exclusion, single-flight/CAS claim, per-process single-flight remain and act as filters on the coordination-ordered candidates.
   - If no entry passes the fresh eligibility check, dispatcher reports `no-candidate` (probe semantics unchanged by `WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7` — coordination file emptiness is a transient offer gap, not a backlog signal).
